jobs.title: Senior Academic Advisor
jobs.description:
About Inspira Education

Inspira Education Group is one of the fastest-growing edtech startups in the US. We started with a simple mission to democratize access to high-quality coaching so that every student in the world has an equal opportunity to access the best opportunities.

As the world’s leading network of top admissions coaches in medical, legal, business, and college studies, we’re building software and services in one place—disrupting long-entrenched application processes with products and experiences that strive to provide an equal platform for candidates from diverse backgrounds worldwide.

As one of the fastest-growing edtech firms in the world, we are backed by some of the leading venture capital firms and investors in the world, including Zeev Ventures, Quiet Capital, Craft Ventures and Jeff Fluhr (Founder of Stubhub).

The Role

We’re currently hiring Senior Academic Advisors across multiple Inspira Education Group brands.

We’re looking for a driven, entrepreneurial Senior Academic Advisor with a strong ownership mindset. Someone who thrives in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment and is eager to help students achieve their academic dreams. You’ll play a key role in driving revenue growth through inbound sales, while also helping to build and refine the systems and processes that will allow our sales function to scale in the future.

This is one of the most impactful roles at Inspira. As the first point of contact for parents and students exploring our programs, you’ll set the tone for their entire experience. The trust, empathy, and expertise you bring to these conversations often become the deciding factors in their choice to work with us. You’ll guide them through one of the most meaningful decisions of their lives- investing in their education and future success.

What You'll Do

  • Lead consultative intro calls (inbound) with parents and students to understand their goals, explain the admissions process, and recommend the right Inspira programs and packages based on their needs
  • Own the relationship with prospective students and families from first touch through enrollment by building trust, offering guidance, and ensuring a smooth and positive experience throughout their journey
  • Follow up strategically and consistently to stay connected with prospects, anticipate questions or concerns, and help them confidently decide to partner with Inspira
  • Experiment and innovate—test new scripts, refine messaging, and explore creative follow-up strategies to maximize conversion rates and continuously improve the enrollment experience
  • Close deals across a range of programs and services, meeting or exceeding monthly and quarterly sales goals
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with the marketing, counseling, and finance teams to ensure seamless handoffs, strong alignment, and an exceptional customer experience
  • Stay informed on competitor offerings and market trends; provide real-time feedback to founders and leadership to shape product, pricing, and go-to-market strategy
  • Leverage HubSpot CRM to manage the full sales cycle—tracking leads, logging communications, creating email templates, forecasting revenue, and maintaining data integrity across all stages
  • Forecast enrollments accurately by managing deal stages, values, and close dates in HubSpot
  • Support onboarding and customer success for newly enrolled students to ensure a strong start and high satisfaction

Who You Are

  • 3–5 years of experience in inbound sales within a service-oriented or consultative environment, ideally with sales cycles under 2–3 months
  • Proven success selling premium or high-value service packages (ACV $5,000+), with a track record of exceeding targets and delivering exceptional client experiences
  • Excellent communication skills. You’re confident presenting, writing, and speaking with clarity, empathy, and professionalism
  • Strong CRM proficiency, preferably in HubSpot (or similar tools), with a knack for maintaining clean data and using systems to drive performance
  • Comfort with data and reporting, including experience using Excel or Google Sheets to build and interpret dashboards
  • Nice to Have: Prior experience in education, admissions, or academic consulting sales

What We Value

As a fast-growing startup, every team member plays a pivotal role in shaping our culture and driving our success. At Inspira, we’re looking for people who embody these core values:

  • Winning Attitude: You find a way to succeed. You dig deeper to understand the “why” behind a no, and you don’t stop until you’ve found a solution
  • Curiosity: You constantly push yourself to learn, experiment, and improve. You’re open to new ideas and you see setbacks as opportunities to grow
  • Genuine Relationships: You lead with empathy and integrity. Parents and students trust us with one of the most important decisions of their lives, and you honor that by building authentic, human connections
  • Smart and Hard Work: You combine awareness and judgment with effort and discipline. You know when to think strategically and when to roll up your sleeves
  • Humility and Teamwork: You celebrate collective success over individual wins. You welcome feedback, learn from mistakes, and support those around you

Why you'll love Inspira

  • Amazing people with a great vision and values
  • Mission-driven team culture focused on student success
  • Your work directly impacts the lives and careers of students across the globe
  • Health, dental, and vision insurance, base plans 100% employer paid
  • Pre-tax benefits (FSA, DCFSA, HSA, Commuter)
  • Flexible paid time off (PTO) and paid holidays
  • 401(k) with company match

Compensation

OTE: $200K+

For more information about our company, please visit our website: Inspira Education Group.

Inspira Education Group does not discriminate based on race, sex, color, religion, age, national origin, marital status, disability, veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other reason prohibited by law in providing employment opportunities and benefits.

For over 20 years, Smartsheet has empowered teams to manage work seamlessly and scale solutions smarter. Now, in our most ambitious chapter yet, we are uniting human teams with AI agents. By orchestrating the work agents do best, automating manual tasks and uncovering insights at scale, we create the space for people to focus on what truly matters: judgment, creativity, and big thinking. That is magic at work, and it’s what we show up for every day.

Smartsheet is seeking a Senior Channel Account Manager to own and grow our business with a named list of strategic channel partners, including large resellers and distributors such as SHI. In this role, you will be the day-to-day owner of each assigned partner relationship: building joint business plans, driving partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline, and turning those relationships into predictable, repeatable revenue across public sector and enterprise customers.

You will work hand in hand with Smartsheet's direct sales, marketing, sales operations, and customer success teams, as well as the partners' own sellers and leadership, to make Smartsheet easy to sell, quote, procure, and renew through the channel. The ideal candidate is a hands-on, execution-focused partner manager who is equally comfortable in a partner QBR with senior leadership and in the details of deal registration, quoting, and contract vehicles.

You will report to the Director, Partnerships and Alliances, AMER. This role is based in the Americas, with a primary location in the Eastern or Central Time Zone.

You Will

  • Own the relationship, strategy, and results for a named list of strategic channel partners, serving as the primary point of contact for partner sales, marketing, operations, and executive stakeholders. Build these relationships in person by traveling regularly to partner offices and showing up at customer events.
  • Develop and execute joint business plans for each named partner with clear revenue targets, pipeline goals, key activities, and quarterly milestones.
  • Drive partner-sourced and partner-influenced bookings to quota, and accurately forecast and manage the partner pipeline in Salesforce.

  • Enable partner sales, pre-sales, and services teams through training, certifications, product launches, and sales plays so that they can confidently position and sell Smartsheet.
  • Plan and execute joint marketing and demand generation programs, including campaigns, events, and webinars, and manage Market Development Funds (MDF) to maximize ROI.

  • Track, analyze, and report on partner performance metrics, including bookings, pipeline coverage, win rates, and enablement progress, to senior leadership.
  • Coordinate cross-functionally with sales, marketing, product, customer success, and finance to resolve partner issues and escalations quickly and professionally.
  • Share market insights, partner feedback, and competitive intelligence to inform Smartsheet's channel strategy, programs, and product direction.

You Have

  • 7+ years of enterprise SaaS sales, channel, or partnerships experience, with at least 4+ years managing channel partners such as VARs, distributors, and resellers.
  • A proven track record of meeting or exceeding revenue quotas through partner-led and co-sell motions.
  • Hands-on experience managing professional services partners, reseller or distributor relationships.

  • Exceptional cross-functional collaboration skills with the ability to align and influence sales, marketing, sales operations, product, and customer success teams.
  • Strong analytical and business acumen, with proficiency in Salesforce.com CRM and Google Suite and comfort with data-driven decision making.
  • Excellent planning, forecasting, and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple partners and priorities in parallel.
  • Strong presentation and communication skills, with the ability to articulate compelling partner value propositions.
  • A consultative approach and a genuine interest in understanding and solving partner business challenges.
  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Sales, or a related field (or equivalent professional experience).
  • Willingness and ability to travel regularly, approximately 25% of the time, as an essential function of the role. You will be expected to be on-site at partner offices for QBRs, planning sessions, and sales team engagements, and to attend customer events, partner conferences, and industry events across the Americas.

jobs.description:
Redwood Automation Engineer (RunMyJobs / SAP BPA), SAP Finance, Lithuania

Contract: Duration being confirmed. Start: 15 November 2026. Location: Remote, for consultants based in Lithuania. Day rate: EUR 350 a day. Language: English.

The programme

An established organisation is automating its finance close on Redwood, connected to SAP. Redwood Finance Automation runs on the same Redwood platform as RunMyJobs. SAP sold that platform for years as SAP Central Process Scheduling (CPS) and later SAP Business Process Automation (BPA). If you have built on it under any of those names, the experience carries straight across.

The work covers the record-to-report cycle: the period-end close, balance sheet reconciliation, accruals and journal posting, all running against SAP. You will build what the solution design sets out and carry each process through testing, go-live and early support.

What you will work on

The close built as Redwood process definitions: task lists, dependencies, parameters and calendars, including SAP factory calendars. Automated steps that run the SAP FI/CO period-end programs in the background, in the right order and with the right variants. Balance sheet reconciliation, accruals and journal posting automated on the platform. Logic in REL and RedwoodScript where the standard designer does not meet the requirement. The connection to SAP S/4HANA or ECC through XBP and RFC. Unit and integration testing, defect fixing, and support through user acceptance testing. Promotion between environments, cutover and hypercare. Technical documentation and handover to the support team.

What you bring

Hands-on build on the Redwood platform under any of its names: RunMyJobs, SAP BPA by Redwood, SAP CPS or Cronacle. You built the process definitions or job chains yourself. REL and RedwoodScript. SAP connections through XBP and RFC on at least one live SAP estate. Knowledge of the SAP FI/CO programs that run at month-end and the order they run in. 5 or more years in SAP automation, job scheduling or finance systems engineering.

Useful but not essential:

A migration from SAP BPA or SAP CPS to RunMyJobs. Redwood Finance Automation (RunMyFinance). SAP Financial Closing cockpit or SAP Advanced Financial Closing. Financial services or another regulated industry, including work under SOX or similar audit controls.

How to respond

Apply with your CV and your available start date. With it, add three lines on your most recent Redwood, SAP CPS or SAP BPA work: what you automated, the SAP system it ran against, and what you built yourself.

Yadimen Consulting Limited is an IT consulting company focused on financial services. For this programme we are putting experienced Redwood and SAP automation people in front of the client.

  • You've scaled a queue-driven or real-time system through an order of magnitude of traffic growth.

jobs.title: Coordinación Senior de Crecimiento - Sistema B Internacional
jobs.description:
Proceso de selección desarrollado por matteria

México - Remoto

Quiénes somos

Organización regional sin fines de lucro especializada en sostenibilidad empresarial e impacto. Trabaja con empresas, aliados, academia, sector público y sociedad civil para promover la adopción de estándares internacionales de gestión, fortalecer prácticas de triple impacto y movilizar colaboración hacia una economía más inclusiva, equitativa y regenerativa. Opera mediante programas de acompañamiento, formación, comunidad, alianzas y acción colectiva en América Latina y el Caribe.

Propósito del cargo

Impulsar el crecimiento de Empresas B en la Región Norte mediante el desarrollo y cierre de alianzas estratégicas con actores empresariales e institucionales que permitan ampliar el alcance del movimiento. La posición combina visión estratégica con ejecución comercial directa, identificando oportunidades, estructurando propuestas y negociando acuerdos que generen nuevas certificaciones. Su responsabilidad es regional desde el inicio, con foco prioritario en México durante el primer año.

Principales Responsabilidades

  • Identificar y priorizar oportunidades de crecimiento: Mapear organizaciones empresariales, gremiales e institucionales con potencial para ampliar la certificación B en la Región Norte, concentrando la ejecución en México durante el primer año, según las oportunidades de cada sector y territorio.

  • Desarrollar relaciones institucionales y empresariales de alto nivel: Establecer y fortalecer vínculos con cámaras de comercio, asociaciones, instituciones públicas, redes empresariales y directivos corporativos, generando oportunidades concretas de colaboración y crecimiento.

  • Estructurar, negociar y cerrar alianzas estratégicas: Identificar las necesidades de potenciales aliados, desarrollar propuestas de valor y programas de colaboración, y liderar su negociación hasta la formalización, en alineación con la Gerencia Regional de Estándares y Crecimiento.

  • Articular la implementación de las alianzas: Coordinar la transferencia y puesta en marcha de los acuerdos formalizados con los equipos responsables, sin asumir la ejecución operativa ni los procesos técnicos de certificación.

  • Gestionar y ampliar la cartera de aliados y oportunidades: Dar continuidad a las relaciones y oportunidades existentes, desarrollar nuevas alianzas mediante prospección propia y articular esfuerzos con Marketing, Country Managers y equipos regionales.

  • Impulsar los indicadores de crecimiento y conversión: Contribuir al incremento de registros en la Evaluación de Impacto B, envíos a certificación y nuevas Empresas B, mediante la generación, negociación y cierre de alianzas estratégicas.

  • Asegurar la trazabilidad de la gestión comercial: Supervisar el seguimiento de oportunidades, acuerdos y compromisos mediante las herramientas de gestión existentes, con apoyo del equipo operativo y visibilidad de los avances y resultados.

  • Representar institucionalmente a Sistema B: Participar y liderar reuniones, espacios de relacionamiento y eventos estratégicos en la Región Norte, con autonomía de gestión, criterio ejecutivo y disponibilidad para viajes frecuentes, estimados en un 30 % del tiempo.

Requisitos y competencias para trabajar con nosotros

Educación

  • Formación profesional en negocios, administración, ingeniería o áreas afines al relacionamiento corporativo.

Experiencia

  • Experiencia comprobable en crecimiento comercial, desarrollo de negocios o venta consultiva B2B de servicios, consultoría, certificaciones o soluciones intangibles.

  • Evidencia de negociación y cierre de acuerdos o programas con aliados, no únicamente prospección o relacionamiento sin resultados.

  • Experiencia trabajando en estructuras matriciales, multiárea o multipaís.

  • Relacionamiento directo con gerencias, equipos ejecutivos, gremios o tomadores de decisión.

  • Conocimiento del mercado empresarial mexicano y de su dinámica institucional.

  • Se valora experiencia en sostenibilidad, ESG, estándares internacionales, ecosistemas empresariales o modelos de membresía.

Conocimientos y habilidades

  • Desarrollo de alianzas B2B, identificación de necesidades, formulación de propuestas, negociación y cierre consultivo.

  • Manejo avanzado de CRM, análisis de pipeline, forecast e indicadores de conversión.

  • Capacidad para comprender y comunicar requisitos técnicos, metodologías y estándares.

  • Español requerido; inglés deseable; portugués valorable.

Competencias

  • Orientación a resultados y disciplina de ejecución: organización, rigurosidad y atención al detalle para gestionar el pipeline, los indicadores, los compromisos y el seguimiento de oportunidades.

  • Comunicación, persuasión e influencia: conversaciones de valor, escucha de necesidades y comunicación asertiva con públicos directivos e institucionales.

  • Priorización y criterio comercial: capacidad para evaluar el potencial, la factibilidad y el impacto de las oportunidades, enfocando los esfuerzos en aquellas con mayor posibilidad de conversión.

  • Autonomía y criterio propio: capacidad para identificar oportunidades, proponer iniciativas y avanzar en su ejecución con seguimiento y responsabilidad, actuando con independencia frente a empresas de cualquier tamaño sin requerir acompañamiento constante.

  • Balance entre apertura relacional y ejecución: capacidad de generar vínculos genuinos con tomadores de decisión sin sacrificar el seguimiento estructurado, el registro disciplinado en CRM y el cierre efectivo de oportunidades.

  • Influencia transversal, colaboración y comunicación con públicos diversos: capacidad para trabajar con diferentes áreas, países y actores, construir acuerdos y coordinar acciones dentro de una estructura matricial.

Perfil de nuestro equipo de trabajo

  • Integridad y rigor en la aplicación de estándares y políticas.

  • Orientación a resultados, datos y compromisos adquiridos.

  • Colaboración efectiva en una estructura regional y matricial.

  • Coherencia entre el propósito de impacto y la sostenibilidad financiera.

Intereses claves para trabajar con nosotros

  • Transformación del sector empresarial mediante prácticas de sostenibilidad e impacto.

  • Expansión de estándares internacionales de gestión y medición.

  • Desarrollo del mercado mexicano y fortalecimiento de soluciones de impacto para empresas.

  • Construcción de una economía más inclusiva, equitativa y regenerativa.

Razones para sumarte a nuestro equipo

  • Liderazgo de una comunidad regional de aproximadamente 360 Empresas B, cifra compartida durante el levantamiento de noviembre de 2026 y sujeta a evolución.

  • Capacidad de definir la experiencia y propuesta de valor para empresas de distintos tamaños, sectores y geografías.

  • Relacionamiento con alta dirección empresarial y articulación de alianzas multisectoriales con impacto regional.

  • Trabajo remoto desde México, flexibilidad de organización del trabajo y colaboración con equipos de varios países.

Detalles relevantes antes de postular a esta vacante

  • La persona debe residir en México.

  • Se requiere disponibilidad para viajes y trabajo con distintos husos horarios.

  • Disponibilidad para viajes nacionales frecuentes y estratégicos (estimados en un 30% del tiempo, equivalente a una semana al mes); movilidad indispensable hacia los principales hubs de crecimiento en México (tales como Guadalajara, Monterrey, Puebla, Baja California o Oaxaca) para la gestión presencial de alianzas con cámaras de comercio, gremios e instituciones públicas.

  • Alcance geográfico: Región Norte de Sistema B Internacional, que comprende México, Colombia, Venezuela, Centroamérica y el Caribe. La posición tiene responsabilidad regional desde su incorporación, con foco prioritario de ejecución en México durante el primer año.

We're looking for an Investor Outreach Specialist to be the first voice real estate investors and homebuyers hear at a growing U.S. mortgage brokerage. You will call warm inbound leads who have asked about investment property or short-term rental financing, build trust quickly, qualify their goals and timeline, and book consultations with the mortgage team while you are still on the phone.

This is a relationship-first sales role, not a dialing-volume role. The leads are warm, and the quality of the conversation is what turns them into attended appointments and funded loans. You will not be reading a script. You will ask good questions, listen, handle objections naturally, and make people feel they are talking to a person who understands their plans. The licensed mortgage team handles loan terms and advice, and your job is to qualify interest and set up the consultation. If you naturally connect with people, think on your feet, and take ownership of results in a performance-driven environment, this role is a strong fit.

Why You'll Want to Join

  • You will be paid in USD (bi-monthly: every 15th and 30th)
  • Performance incentives on top of base pay, including commission for attended consultations and for funded loans from your appointments
  • Paid Time Off in accordance with company policy
  • Observance of Holidays per company guidelines
  • 100% remote setup so you can work wherever you're most productive
  • This role requires availability during US business hours, with the main calling window in the late afternoon and early evening Eastern Time
  • Work with a growing, relationship-focused brokerage serving real estate investors
  • Ongoing coaching, and a role where quality of conversation matters more than call counts

What You'll Work On

Warm Lead Conversations

  • Contact warm inbound leads who have requested information about investment properties or short-term rentals
  • Build trust and rapport within the first few minutes of every conversation
  • Ask thoughtful discovery questions to understand each prospect's goals and timeline
  • Handle common objections calmly and naturally without sounding scripted

Qualification and Booking

  • Qualify prospective borrowers and investors before scheduling appointments
  • Schedule qualified consultations directly on the mortgage specialist's calendar while still on the phone
  • Coordinate with the mortgage team to give them useful context before every consultation

Follow-Up and CRM

  • Maintain detailed, accurate CRM notes after every interaction

  • Keep pipeline records organized so nothing is lost between a first call and a funded loan

How Success Is Measured

  • High-quality conversations and qualified appointments booked
  • Appointment show rate
  • CRM accuracy, organization, and consistent follow-up
  • Professional communication and contribution to funded loans
  • Quality always comes before quantity

What You Bring

  • The ability to build rapport quickly with strangers, think on your feet, and adapt the conversation naturally
  • Strong questioning and listening skills
  • Calm, professional objection handling
  • Organized habits and a record of documenting every interaction accurately
  • Coachability: you learn quickly and enjoy feedback
  • Ownership of results and comfort in a performance-driven environment
  • Dependable, punctual, and highly professional
  • Reliable high-speed internet and a quiet work environment
  • Available to work full-time during US business hours, including the late afternoon and early evening Eastern Time calling window

Nice to Have

  • Experience in real estate sales, the mortgage industry, loan processing, or real estate investing
  • Experience in business development, investor relations, or financial services
  • Experience with CRMs such as Bonzo, GoHighLevel, HubSpot, or Salesforce

jobs.title: Associate Director, AP New Course Product Development
jobs.description:
Associate Director, AP New Course Product Development

College Board – AP&I

Location:

  • This is a remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office). All CB employees are required to occasionally travel to meet in person for business purposes.

Role Type:

  • This is a full-time term position that will last for 2 years from the start date.

About the Team

AP® is a rigorous academic program built on the commitment, passion, and hard work of students and educators from secondary schools and higher education. With 40+ courses in a wide variety of subject areas, AP provides willing and academically prepared high school students with the opportunity to study and learn at the college level.

Through the New Course Initiative, the AP Publications team is partnering with the larger AP Program to expand the course portfolio, with several new courses currently in development. The team consists of professionals with expertise in a variety of domains that are integral to the editorial development and production of AP course products. The team builds the publications that bring each new course to life: Course Frameworks (CFs), Course and Exam Descriptions (CEDs), Practice Exams (PEs), and teacher- and student-facing course resources such as project-based learning (PBL) implementation guides and project guides. The team partners closely with course experts, development committees, editors, and outside vendors to deliver clear, accurate, high-quality materials on schedule.

About the Opportunity

As Associate Director, AP New Course Product Development, you will play a key role in moving new AP course publications from early drafts through final page proofs. You will build and prepare turnover manuscripts for CFs, CEDs, and course resources; keep publication schedules accurate and visible to everyone who depends on them; plan and support meetings with course stakeholders; and serve as a reliable point of contact for AP colleagues and outside vendors. As priorities shift, you will also lend the same type of support to existing AP courses.

This is an ideal opportunity for a highly organized, detail-oriented early career professional who enjoys the craft of publishing, thrives in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment, and is motivated by mission-driven work in service of expanding access to college-level learning.

In this role, you will:

Build Manuscripts, Support Page Reviews, and Deliver Final Files for New Course Publications and Resources (40%)

  • Prepare and assemble turnover manuscripts for CFs, CEDs, PE, and course resources (PBL guides, project guides, and related materials) using approved templates, styles, and AP editorial conventions
  • Incorporate content, reviewer, and editorial revisions accurately across iterative drafts, maintaining clean version control
  • Track and prepare supporting elements, such as graphics requests, permissions, and sample exam item delivery, so manuscripts are complete at handoff
  • Perform quality checks, including copy-to-copy comparisons and consistency checks, before manuscripts move to editorial review or paging
  • Perform cross-check reviews of PDF page proofs to verify that edits from prior rounds were made accurately and completely
  • Consolidate stakeholder and leadership review comments onto a single revision PDF for the external vendor, flagging conflicting feedback for resolution and ensuring each edit is clear and actionable
  • Close the loop on each publication by delivering final approved content and files to the appropriate teams for posting

Manage Schedules and Coordinate Stakeholder Meetings (25%)

  • Track and maintain publication schedules for assigned new courses, keeping milestones, dependencies, and owners current in Smartsheet
  • Flag schedule risks early and propose options to keep milestones on track
  • Plan and coordinate meetings with key course stakeholders, including course experts and cross-divisional collaborators; prepare agendas and materials, capture notes, and follow up on action items
  • Document decisions in a shared, easy-to-find location so course teams can access current information independently

Maintain Stakeholder and Vendor Correspondence (20%)

  • Serve as a reliable point of contact for AP stakeholders and outside vendors (such as compositors and production partners), ensuring consistent communication, tracking of deliverables, and clarity of ownership
  • Prepare turnovers, review requests, and revision instructions; confirm receipt and track turnaround times
  • Maintain correspondence and decision logs for each assigned course
  • Elevate issues to the appropriate lead and help steer them to resolution

Support Revised AP Courses and Continuous Improvement (15%)

  • Provide manuscript, page review, scheduling, and coordination support for revised AP courses as priorities and capacity require
  • Deliver final approved content and files for revised courses to the appropriate teams for posting
  • Ramp quickly into unfamiliar course content and conventions as assignments shift
  • Contribute to a culture of continuous improvement by building checklists, job aids, and templates, and by exploring approved generative AI tools that make manuscript work more efficient and consistent

About You

To qualify for this role, you must have:

  • 3+ years of experience in publishing, editorial, or project coordination, ideally with educational materials, and a bachelor's degree
  • Excellent organizational, time management, and project coordination skills and the demonstrated ability to move forward multiple projects in concert while meeting timelines
  • Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, Adobe Acrobat, and Smartsheet (working knowledge of Adobe InDesign and SharePoint is preferred)
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills 
  • Strong attention to detail
  • A growth mindset and flexibility when working through ambiguity and shifting priorities in a dynamic, collaborative setting 
  • Ability to operate independently, anticipate needs, and take initiative while building strong partnerships across teams and levels of seniority 
  • The ability to travel 2-4 times per year to College Board offices or on behalf of College Board business

All roles at College Board require:

  • A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work
  • Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort with learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively.
  • Clear and concise communication skills, written and verbal
  • A learner's mindset and a commitment to growth: welcoming diverse perspectives, giving and receiving timely, respectful feedback, and continuously improving through iterative learning and user input.
  • A drive for impact and excellence: solving complex problems, making data-informed decisions, prioritizing what matters most, and continuously improving through learning, user input, and external benchmarking.
  • A collaborative and empathetic approach: working across differences, fostering trust, and contributing to a culture of shared success
  • Authorization to work in the United States

About Our Process

  • Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of 5 business days.
  • While the hiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter video screen, hiring manager interview, performance exercise, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership and reference checks.

What We Offer

At College Board, we offer more than a paycheck: we provide a meaningful career, a supportive team, and a comprehensive package designed to help you thrive. We’re a self-sustaining nonprofit that believes in fair and competitive compensation grounded in your qualifications, experience, impact, and the market.

A Thoughtful Approach to Compensation

  • The hiring range for this role is $56,000–$85,000.
  • Your exact salary will depend on your location, experience, and how your background compares to others in similar roles at the College Board.
  • We aim to make our best offer upfront, rooted in fairness, transparency, and market data.
  • We adjust salaries by location to ensure fairness, no matter where you live.

You’ll have open, transparent conversations about compensation, benefits, and what it’s like to work at College Board throughout your hiring process. Check out our careers page for more.

jobs.title: ISU Specialist - Remote
jobs.description:
SUMMARY:

The Investigative Services Unit Specialist is a Subject Matter Expert (SME) on potential fraud cases and related investigative activities affecting AF Group. The primary function of the ISU Specialist is to detect and deter insurance fraud and to use developed knowledge, skills, and abilities to support the mission of AF Group and comply with state regulatory requirements. The Specialist will effectively manage day-to-day investigative assignments by providing timely, quality, and cost-effective investigative results to field staff. When potential fraud cases are identified, the Specialist will conduct thorough investigations, document results, coordinate mitigation strategies, make appropriate recommendations, and required notifications.

Under the direction of the ISU Director, this position is responsible for fraud investigations, compliance with state regulatory requirements, liaison with law enforcement, anti-fraud training, and ISU quality assurance. Investigations could include complex financial fraud and organized fraud-ring schemes. The ISU Specialist directs vendor investigations, examines investigative reports, reviews surveillance video, and determines if further investigation is warranted. The Investigative Specialist will review vendor invoices for accuracy and contract compliance. The Specialist collaborates with stakeholders to coordinate mitigation strategies and risk management. The ISU Specialist is responsible for educating internal and external customers on the department’s capabilities and effectiveness and provides training on reporting potential fraud.

RESPONSIBILITIES/TASKS:

  • Communicates and collaborates with departmental stakeholders to promote open lines of communication and appropriate referrals for investigation.
  • Assess, triage, and prioritize referrals received to develop investigative plan.
  • Direct, communicate, and manage work assigned to investigative vendors.
  • Analyze intelligence information and make determination for further investigation utilizing available resources, knowledge of fraud schemes and investigation strategies.
  • Conduct investigations to include desk and field investigations, and interviews of involved parties. Obtain, review, and analyze relevant documents and records.
  • Fraud investigations conducted to include claimants, medical and ancillary providers, premium avoidance, and other schemes related to workers compensation, property, casualty, commercial auto, trucking, and surplus coverage.
  • Coordinate and direct onsite investigation of catastrophic claim incidents as requested by claim adjustors.
  • Prepares comprehensive investigation reports and documents all findings and developments in the case management system.
  • Comply with all state regulations related to reporting potential fraud.
  • Conducts follow-up on fraud referrals and monitors the status of a case through prosecution. Testifies in court proceedings when required.
  • Responds to subpoena and other external record requests in accordance with AF Group procedures.
  • Determines loss incurred and seek restitution or civil recovery.
  • Assesses investigative results to determine savings achieved.
  • Establishes and maintains external relationships with law enforcement, trade organizations and others involved in the investigation of insurance fraud.
  • Consistently monitors workflows to maximize efficiency.
  • Monitor vendor performance standards and service levels. May make recommendations for metrics used to measure vendor performance.
  • Analyzes trends and completes comprehensive and detailed reports.
  • Reconcile vendor billing and follow up with accounts payable/vendors regarding vendor accounting issues.
  • Evaluates training needs and designs and develops training modules, materials and evaluations related to fraud for internal and external customers as needed.
  • Maintains up-to-date technical knowledge of investigative core functions.
  • Deliver presentations as needed.
  • Use independent judgment in all areas of responsibility, while considering department and division priorities.
  • Coordinates with enterprise companies in the development and management of ISU.
  • Additional duties and projects assigned.

This position description identifies the responsibilities and tasks typically associated with the performance of the job. Other relevant essential functions may be required.

EMPLOYMENT QUALIFICATIONS:

EDUCATION OR EQUIVALENT EXPERIENCE:

Bachelor’s degree in business, criminal justice, law enforcement, insurance, or related field of education required. Knowledge of insurance fraud and other relevant civil and criminal laws is preferred. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered in lieu of degree, preference given to degree. Continuous learning required, as defined by the Company’s learning philosophy. Certification, or progress toward, highly preferred and encouraged.

EXPERIENCE:

With proper education credentials, minimum of seven years of law enforcement and/or insurance claims investigations required. Workers’ compensation experience and/or experience in a property/casualty insurance organization preferred.

SKILLS/KNOWLEDGE/ABILITIES (SKA) REQUIRED:

  1. Strong interpersonal and superior communication skills Must be customer oriented and able to represent the department in meetings with internal and external stakeholders.
  2. Strong writing skills with proven ability to synthesize and document complex case investigation results and prepare presentations.
  3. Demonstrated leadership abilities.
  4. Ability to work independently and collaborate on group projects.
  5. Strong knowledge of laws, regulations, and compliance requirements related to insurance.
  6. Demonstrated technical knowledge of insurance administration, claims management, or relevant insurance expertise.
  7. Strong background in word processing, spreadsheets, and graphics programs required with knowledge of Microsoft applications preferred.
  8. Ability to analyze and synthesize large data sets and complex policy, financial and medical records.
  9. Ability to analyze and interpret documents for accuracy in reference to technical, legal, and financial information.
  10. Ability to effectively exchange information clearly and concisely, present ideas, report facts, and other information, and respond to questions as appropriate, both in oral and written communications.
  11. Ability to quickly make decisions and comprehend the consequences of various problem situations and take appropriate actions and/or refer problems for necessary decision making.
  12. Ability to organize and prioritize multiple assignments.
  13. Ability to maintain confidentiality,
  14. Ability to perform other assignments at locations outside the office.
  15. Ability to work with minimal supervision.

WORKING CONDITIONS:

Work is performed in a home setting with no unusual hazards. Occasional travel required. Must possess a valid driver’s license with a record that meets corporate standards. Work is required at various times of the day and sometimes weekend work may be required.

PAY RANGE:
Actual compensation decision relies on the consideration of internal equity, candidate’s skills and professional experience, geographic location, market, and other potential factors. It is not standard practice for an offer to be at or near the top of the range, and therefore a reasonable estimate for this role is between $73,600 - $123,200.

jobs.title: Freight Dispatcher — Load Exceptions & Service Recovery
jobs.description:
Freight Dispatcher — Load Exceptions & Service Recovery

Full-Time | Remote — United States | U.S. Freight Operations

When Freight Plans Change, Keep the Operation Moving

We are hiring a Freight Dispatcher — Load Exceptions & Service Recovery to support U.S. trucking operations with a focus on shipment delays, service exceptions, changing appointments, driver communication, and operational follow-up.

Freight does not always move according to the original plan. Drivers encounter facility delays, appointment changes, traffic, weather, equipment problems, Hours-of-Service limitations, and other situations that require accurate information and timely coordination.

This position may be a strong fit for transportation professionals, including experienced or former CDL-A drivers, who understand how quickly operating conditions can change and how important clear communication becomes when they do.

Previous employment specifically under the title of Freight Dispatcher is not required. Applicants must have relevant U.S. trucking, transportation, logistics, fleet, or closely related operational experience.

Load Exception Management

  • Monitor active freight for delays, missed check-ins, appointment changes, and service exceptions.
  • Identify missing information and determine what additional details are needed.
  • Gather accurate updates from drivers, brokers, shippers, receivers, and authorized transportation personnel.
  • Document delays and changing shipment conditions promptly.
  • Identify situations requiring operational, safety, compliance, or management escalation.
  • Maintain clear records of outstanding issues and required follow-up.
  • Continue monitoring assigned exceptions until the appropriate operational action has been completed.

Service Recovery & Coordination

  • Assist with coordinating revised pickup or delivery appointments when authorized.
  • Communicate verified changes to drivers and applicable transportation personnel.
  • Evaluate how delays may affect subsequent appointments or freight assignments.
  • Assist with identifying workable next steps when an original transportation plan changes.
  • Coordinate routine recovery actions within assigned authority.
  • Escalate decisions requiring additional authorization.
  • Avoid making commitments regarding freight, appointments, rates, or service outcomes outside assigned authority.

Driver & Broker Communication

  • Communicate professionally with U.S. CDL-A drivers, freight brokers, shippers, receivers, and transportation personnel.
  • Request accurate driver and shipment-status information.
  • Communicate verified appointment and operational changes.
  • Maintain professional telephone, email, and digital communication.
  • Document significant communications and outstanding actions.
  • Escalate broker-verification, safety, service, documentation, or compliance concerns when appropriate.

Freight & Load Support

  • Use DAT One, Truckstop, or comparable U.S. freight load boards when assigned.
  • Review available freight according to lane, equipment type, mileage, appointments, and operating requirements.
  • Calculate loaded mileage, deadhead mileage, total trip mileage, and rate per mile.
  • Consider driver availability and Hours of Service when evaluating alternative freight options.
  • Present appropriate freight information for authorized review and booking.
  • Negotiate freight rates only when specifically authorized.

Transportation Documentation

  • Maintain accurate load and dispatch records.
  • Review rate confirmations and applicable shipment instructions.
  • Maintain bills of lading, proof-of-delivery documents, and related transportation records.
  • Document appointment changes, delays, detention, layover, TONU, and other applicable freight exceptions.
  • Maintain accurate communication histories and operational notes.
  • Identify missing or inconsistent information requiring follow-up.

Required Transportation Background

Relevant professional experience may include:

  • CDL-A truck driving
  • Freight dispatch support
  • Fleet operations
  • Carrier operations
  • Transportation coordination
  • Logistics operations
  • Freight brokerage support

jobs.description:
about us:

Spectrum.Life is a whole-of-health digital partner that guides organisations and their people to thrive, delivering clinically backed digital health, mental health and wellbeing solutions.

Our HealthTech delivers digital transformation for Insurers, Educators and Employers through Co-creation or seamlessly integrated out-of-the-box solutions, that decrease digital fragmentation and engage, empower, and transform their people’s lives.

Established in 2018 by Stuart McGoldrick and Stephen Costello, Spectrum.Life provides services internationally to over 7.2m insurance members, 3,000 corporate clients, 60 universities and 650,000 university students. Spectrum.Life currently employs over 450 people.

Our vision is to change and save as many lives as possible.

role brief:

The HCPC Clinical and Counselling Psychologists Digital Therapist role is ideal for HCPC Registered Clinical and Counselling Psychologists Chartered with BPS. This position is a vital part of the Spectrum mental health team, delivering evidence-based psychological talking therapies digitally (video, phone, text) You will be responsible for delivering psychological talking therapies, evidence based, high-intensity interventions while adhering to our clinical governance frameworks to ensure effective and safe care.

responsibilities:

  • Deliver Psychological Evidence-Based Interventions
  • Provide high-intensity CBT (HI-CBT) and other structured evidence-based interventions digitally (video, phone, text-based).
  • Deliver NICE-recommended therapies, including:
  • Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
  • Compassion-Focused Therapy (CFT)
  • Eye Movement Desensitisation and Reprocessing (EMDR)
  • Counselling for Depression (CfD)
  • Interpersonal Therapy (IPT)
  • Behavioural Activation (BA)
  • Mindfulness-Based Interventions
  • Tailor individualised treatment plans based on client needs and NICE guidelines.
  • Adapt interventions for remote delivery, ensuring therapeutic effectiveness in a digital format.
  • Determine appropriate treatment pathways within a stepped-care model.
  • Utilise Spectrum.Life digital platforms to deliver structured psychological therapies.
  • Guide clients in engaging with self-help tools, psychoeducation, and digital therapy resources.
  • Maintain a therapeutic alliance and client engagement in a remote setting.
  • Work within clinical governance frameworks to ensure safe, ethical, and effective digital therapy.
  • Adhere to data protection (GDPR), confidentiality, and safeguarding policies.
  • Engage in regular clinical supervision, CPD, and peer consultation.
  • Participate in clinical audits, data analysis, and outcome evaluations to enhance service effectiveness.
  • Provide feedback on digital service improvements to enhance client engagement.
  • Support the development of mental health tools and online therapy innovations.

requirements:

  • Full accreditation and registration with: British Psychological Society (BPS) and Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) (both are mandatory)
  • Doctoral Training: Completion of a Doctorate in Clinical Psychology (DClinPsy) or Doctorate in Counselling Psychology (DCPsych).
  • (DCPsych) accredited by the BPS and approved by the HCPC.
  • Minimum of two years post-doctoral qualification experience.
  • Proven experience delivering High-Intensity CBT in IAPT or another relevant service.
  • Experience providing other evidence-based psychological therapies in line with NICE guidelines (e.g., IPT, ACT, EMDR, BA, CFT, CfD).
    Experience working within an IAPT or stepped-care model.
  • Experience in working with adults and children 6+ therapeutically.
  • Experience in screening adults and children, assessing risk, and implementing safety plans.
  • Strong digital literacy skills and the ability to adapt interventions for online platforms.
  • Experience using video conferencing software for therapy delivery (e.g., Microsoft Teams, Zoom).
  • Proficiency in clinical case management systems (CSM) for record-keeping and reporting.
  • Familiarity with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Teams), email, and internet-based tools.
  • A clean record with the associated regulatory body (HCPC for Clinical and Counselling Psychologists).
  • Strong understanding of clinical governance, GDPR, and safeguarding procedures.
  • Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently while contributing to a multidisciplinary team.
  • Strong ability to plan, organise, and prioritise workload efficiently.
  • A commitment to continuous professional development (CPD) and clinical supervision.
  • Ability to work afternoons and evenings, supporting clients in different time zones if required.

desirable:

Experience delivering evidence-based trauma therapies, including:

  • Eye Movement Desensitisation and Reprocessing (EMDR)
  • Trauma-Focused Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (TF-CBT)
  • Trauma-Informed Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (TI-CBT)
  • Compassion-Focused Therapy (CFT)
  • Clinical Supervision
Experience in delivering remote therapy in digital mental health services and Experience working with standardised mental health measures, such as:
  • CBT-Adapted Rating Scale (CBTRS)
  • Generalised Anxiety Disorder Scale (GAD-7)
  • Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9)
  • Additional relevant measures include:
  • Work and Social Adjustment Scale (WSAS)
  • Core Outcome Measures (COMs)
  • Depression Anxiety Stress Scales (DASS-21)
  • Generalised Anxiety Disorder (GAD-7)
  • Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS)
  • Trauma Symptom Checklist (TSC-40)
  • Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder Checklist (PCL-5)

what are the benefits of working at spectrum.life?

  • Competitive hourly rate of £50 per hour
  • Guaranteed hours

  • Minimum three-month assignment, with options to roll over
  • Remote working
  • Induction, training and a clinician handbook so you can start quickly

jobs.description:
ROLE TITLE

Real Estate Executive VA - Administrative Operations & CRM Support

Ready to be the person who keeps three busy real estate partners organized, their leads moving, and their business running smoothly behind the scenes?

We're looking for a sharp, proactive, and experienced Real Estate Executive VA who can take ownership of administrative operations, manage Compass CRM, and ensure important opportunities don't get lost in the day-to-day workload.

If you know your way around Compass, can manage multiple moving pieces without constant reminders, and take pride in keeping every lead, follow-up, document, and task accounted for, this could be your next role.

Pro tip: Applications that include a short introduction video highlighting your real estate experience and hands-on Compass CRM background are strongly encouraged. Be prepared to demonstrate your actual Compass knowledge during the selection process.

This is a fully remote role supporting a U.S.-based residential real estate team. You'll communicate professionally with three managing partners and coordinate closely with their existing ISA and Transaction Coordinator during the client's designated U.S. business hours.

This is not an entry-level real estate VA position. STK will provide orientation on its internal processes and team procedures, but will not provide foundational Compass training. You must have actual, hands-on experience using Compass CRM and be able to work with it confidently from the start. Candidates without this experience should not apply.

CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Executive and Administrative Support

  • When emails and correspondence arrive for the three managing partners, review, organize, prioritize, and flag items requiring their attention.
  • Draft routine client and business communications for review or coordination, using the team's established communication practices.
  • When appointments, meetings, or scheduling requests arise, coordinate calendars and communicate scheduling details to the appropriate people.
  • Track pending administrative assignments, identify approaching deadlines, and follow up before outstanding items become overdue.
  • Maintain organized records, business documents, and operational information so the partners can retrieve what they need without searching through scattered communications.
  • When routine administrative needs arise, identify the next action and handle it within your authority instead of waiting for step-by-step instructions.
  • Escalate matters requiring a managing partner's judgment rather than making unauthorized client, business, or transaction decisions.

2. Compass CRM Management and Administration

  • Independently navigate and operate Compass CRM and the associated Compass platforms used by the team.
  • When new contacts, prospects, or leads enter the business, create or update the appropriate CRM records and maintain accurate contact information.
  • Monitor leads generated through website inquiries, QR codes, property signage, and other sources.
  • When a lead enters the CRM, review its available information, maintain the appropriate record, and ensure the required follow-up activity is documented.
  • Create and manage CRM tasks, reminders, activities, and follow-up records according to established workflows.
  • Maintain contact notes and communication histories so the managing partners can understand previous interactions and outstanding next steps.
  • Set up buyer property searches and appropriate notifications using the team's established Compass workflows.
  • Support the team's existing CRM processes and ensure that leads, contact records, and follow-up activities are not left incomplete.
  • Review assigned CRM records for missing information, outdated details, and outstanding activities, and correct issues within your authority.

Mandatory execution standard: You must already know how to use Compass CRM in a real estate operating environment. General CRM experience, familiarity with other real estate platforms, or willingness to learn Compass does not meet this requirement.

3. Lead Management and Follow-Up Coordination

  • Monitor incoming buyer and seller inquiries and ensure they are recorded and directed to the appropriate real estate partner.
  • Organize prospects according to their current status, interaction history, and required follow-up.
  • When prospects are not immediately ready to transact, maintain their follow-up schedules and coordinate longer-term nurturing activities.
  • Assist with approved email outreach and client communications.
  • Maintain follow-up schedules for networking contacts, referrals, and prospective clients.
  • When a prospect requires partner involvement, communicate the relevant context and next action rather than simply forwarding an unorganized contact record.
  • Track assigned follow-up activities and identify overdue or missed engagements before they become neglected leads.
  • Maintain consistent engagement throughout the sales pipeline using the team's approved processes.

This role requires active follow-through. Updating a CRM record without ensuring that its required next action is accounted for is not sufficient.

4. Inside Sales Agent (ISA) Support

  • When the ISA requires prospecting information, research and compile relevant contact lists for the team's existing lead-generation activities.
  • Prepare organized prospect lists covering potential sellers, distressed properties, builders, attorneys, and other relevant real estate contacts.
  • Maintain accurate prospect information and corresponding lead records in Compass CRM.
  • Coordinate prospect list delivery, corrections, and updates with the existing ISA.
  • Track administrative aspects of lead-generation activities and maintain the information needed for reporting.

Scope clarification: You are supporting the ISA's administrative and prospecting requirements. You are not replacing the team's existing cold-calling function.

5. Real Estate Listing and Buyer Support

  • When new property listings need administrative preparation, enter and update listing information using the team's approved systems.
  • Organize property details, listing information, and supporting documentation.
  • Maintain listing records and make administrative updates as required.
  • When a prospective buyer needs property options, set up and maintain the appropriate buyer searches in Compass.
  • Prepare real estate forms, contracts, and related documentation using approved templates and under the appropriate supervision.
  • Coordinate required information and document handoffs with the existing Transaction Coordinator.
  • Monitor administrative requirements associated with new listings and buyer inquiries, and follow up on missing information or incomplete handoffs.
  • Keep administrative records organized so that listing and buyer-related work can progress without avoidable documentation delays.

6. Email Marketing and Client Nurturing

  • Assist with creating, scheduling, and managing email marketing campaigns.
  • Build and maintain email nurturing sequences using Flodesk and other approved platforms.
  • Organize client and prospect lists for targeted communications.
  • Support email blasts, action plans, and recurring client engagement campaigns.
  • Execute approved marketing workflows and configure practical automation for repetitive communications where applicable.
  • Coordinate campaign content and scheduling with the team.
  • Maintain accurate audience lists and follow the team's approved campaign instructions.

7. Process Execution and Workflow Improvement

  • Follow the team's established Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) when completing recurring administrative and operational activities.
  • Execute documented workflows consistently rather than creating individual workarounds that bypass established procedures.
  • When repetitive administrative work creates unnecessary manual effort, identify the activity and suggest practical opportunities for automation or process improvement.
  • Use approved AI-assisted tools, including Claude where applicable, to improve administrative efficiency.
  • Maintain operational checklists and tracking systems used to monitor recurring responsibilities.
  • Coordinate with Scale Virtually's Process Engineering Team when process updates or workflow adjustments are required.
  • Communicate workflow issues when existing instructions are incomplete, conflicting, or preventing accurate execution.

8. Reporting and Accountability

  • Submit structured Start-of-Day (SOD) and End-of-Day (EOD) reports.
  • At the start of the workday, communicate priorities and identify outstanding items requiring attention.
  • At the end of the workday, report completed activities, pending tasks, and outstanding follow-ups.
  • Maintain visibility into CRM updates, lead management activities, and important administrative responsibilities.
  • Track assigned work through completion and communicate potential delays before deadlines are affected.
  • Escalate urgent matters to the appropriate managing partner promptly.
  • Keep communication clear and specific so the partners can identify what has been completed, what remains outstanding, and where their involvement is needed.

REQUIREMENTS (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

Candidates must meet ALL of the following:

  1. Hands-on Compass experience: Previous direct experience using Compass's real estate platforms, particularly Compass CRM, in an actual real estate working environment. Experience with other CRMs alone does not qualify.
  2. Immediate Compass readiness: Able to independently perform relevant Compass CRM activities without foundational platform training.
  3. Relevant real estate experience: Previous work as a Real Estate Virtual Assistant, Real Estate Executive Assistant, or Real Estate Administrative Assistant.
  4. Residential real estate knowledge: Understands residential real estate terminology and administrative workflows, including buyer inquiries, seller prospects, property listings, and transaction-related documentation.
  5. CRM and lead management: Has personally maintained CRM records, organized leads, documented interactions, and coordinated follow-up activities.
  6. Listing and buyer administration: Has experience supporting property listing administration and buyer-related workflows.
  7. Executive support capability: Can support multiple executives while keeping priorities, communications, and task ownership organized.
  8. Independent execution: Can complete established administrative workflows without daily instructions, constant checking, or repeated reminders.
  9. Professional English communication: Can communicate clearly and professionally in written and spoken English with managing partners, prospects, the ISA, and the Transaction Coordinator.
  10. Recordkeeping accuracy: Maintains accurate contact records, notes, documents, follow-up tasks, and operational information.
  11. SOP compliance: Can follow documented processes and identify when clarification or escalation is necessary.
  12. Professional judgment: Can handle sensitive client information discreetly and recognize when a matter requires partner approval.

Important: Candidates who have never used Compass CRM hands-on will not proceed, regardless of their general real estate VA experience.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience supporting a multi-agent residential real estate team.
  • Experience using Flodesk or similar email marketing platforms.
  • Familiarity with Claude or other AI-assisted productivity tools.
  • Experience with lead nurturing campaigns and CRM automation.
  • Previous coordination with Inside Sales Agents and Transaction Coordinators.
  • Familiarity with buyer searches, MLS-related workflows, and listing administration.
  • Experience working within structured, process-driven real estate organizations.

TOOLS

Required proficiency:

  • Compass CRM
  • Associated Compass real estate platforms used by the team

Additional platforms and tools:

  • Flodesk
  • Claude
  • Other approved AI-assisted productivity tools
  • Other approved email marketing and administrative platforms

Candidates must distinguish between tools they have actually used and tools they have only encountered or studied.

WHAT WE ACTUALLY CARE ABOUT

  • You can use Compass without being taught the basics. You have performed real CRM work and can explain exactly how you managed contacts, leads, activities, and buyer searches.
  • You close administrative loops. When a lead needs follow-up, a document is missing, or an appointment needs coordination, you track it until the next required action is completed or properly escalated.
  • You can manage three partners without creating three times the supervision. You organize competing priorities and make routine decisions within your authority.
  • Your CRM records are reliable. The partners and ISA can look at a record and understand the prospect's history, current status, and next action.
  • You communicate problems before they become operational failures. You do not wait until a missed deadline or neglected lead becomes someone else's emergency.
  • You execute consistently and improve intelligently. You follow SOPs, maintain reporting discipline, and identify practical opportunities to reduce repetitive work.

WHAT THIS ROLE IS NOT

  • This is not a general virtual assistant position for someone whose only experience is calendar management, inbox management, or basic data entry.
  • This is not a Compass training opportunity. Candidates who need someone to teach them how Compass CRM works are not qualified.
  • This is not an Inside Sales Agent or cold-calling position. The team already has an ISA.
  • This is not a Transaction Coordinator position. You will support listing and buyer administration and coordinate documentation handoffs with the existing Transaction Coordinator.
  • This is not a passive administrative role. You are expected to own assigned workflows, monitor outstanding tasks, and follow through without constant supervision.

POSITION DETAILS

  • Work Arrangement: Fully remote.
  • Employment Structure: Virtual Assistant / independent contractor engagement.
  • Preferred Schedule: Full-time, 40 hours per week.
  • Alternative Schedule: Part-time, 20 hours per week, may be considered.
  • Working Hours: Must be available during STK's designated U.S. business hours. The applicable U.S. time zone and agreed schedule will be confirmed during engagement.
  • Weekend Availability: May be requested depending on operational requirements and the mutually agreed schedule.
  • Work Environment: Performance-driven, remote, and process-oriented. The role requires consistent communication, structured reporting, independent task ownership, and coordination across multiple team members.

APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS

Applications must demonstrate actual, hands-on Compass experience.

Please submit:

  1. Your updated resume, including the real estate teams or professionals you have supported and the administrative responsibilities you personally handled.
  2. A description of your direct experience with Compass CRM. Specify how you used it to manage contacts, incoming leads, follow-up tasks, buyer searches, and listing administration.
  3. The approximate duration and context of your Compass experience. State whether you used Compass directly in a professional role or only encountered it through training or demonstrations.
  4. Your experience supporting multiple real estate agents, partners, or executives.
  5. Your experience with Flodesk, email nurturing, lead management, and coordination with ISAs or Transaction Coordinators.
  6. Your availability for 20 or 40 hours per week and your ability to work during the client's designated U.S. business hours.

Compass proficiency will be validated during recruitment through a practical assessment using a permitted demonstration environment or a scenario-based walkthrough. Candidates must be able to explain their actual platform experience. STK will not provide foundational Compass software training.

PERFORMANCE EXPECTATIONS

Success in this role will be evaluated through observable execution:

  1. Immediate Compass readiness: Performs assigned Compass-related activities independently without basic platform instruction.
  2. Administrative efficiency: Reliably assumes recurring administrative responsibilities from all three managing partners.
  3. CRM accuracy: Maintains complete, accurate, and organized contact and prospect records.
  4. Lead follow-up consistency: Ensures assigned leads have documented follow-up activities and appropriate next steps.
  5. Operational reliability: Completes assigned work on schedule and escalates issues before they affect operations.
  6. Communication: Coordinates effectively with the managing partners, ISA, and Transaction Coordinator.
  7. Process compliance: Follows established workflows, documentation standards, and reporting requirements.

POSITION OBJECTIVE

Provide STK's three managing partners with a dependable, experienced, Compass-proficient Real Estate Executive VA who can immediately take ownership of recurring administrative operations, maintain reliable CRM records, coordinate lead management, and support listing and buyer administration.

The intended result is fewer administrative interruptions for the partners, more consistent prospect follow-up, reliable operational records, and stronger execution across the team's existing real estate workflows.

Benefits

  • Paid Time Off
  • HMO
  • Fully Remote Work

If you are a current Staff, Faculty or Temporary employee at the University of Miami, please click here to log in to Workday to use the internal application process. To learn how to apply for a faculty or staff position, please review this tip sheet.

The Office of the Executive Dean for Research (EDR) based in the Miller School of Medicine (MSOM), has an exciting opportunity for a full-time Senior Manager, Sponsored Programs to work Hybrid or Remote in Miami, FL.


CORE JOB SUMMARY

This role supports the research mission of the University of Miami, MSOM, and the goals of the Executive Dean for Research Office. Applicants must have relevant federal grant administration experience with federal sponsors such as: NIH, DOD, NSF, to be considered for this role.


The Senior Manager, Sponsored Programs directs and oversees all administrative and financial aspects of the Sponsored Programs division at the assigned facilities. The Senior Manager, Sponsored Programs operates with the goals of increasing sponsored funding levels and the output of funding proposal, as well as maximizing the use and efficacy of existing research funding dollars. Further, the incumbent develops and implements policies and methods that further these goals.


CORE JOB FUNCTIONS

  • Identifies potential donors or sources of funding and plans outreach strategies.
  • Participates in the development of grants applications and proposals.
  • Schedules and oversees planning for special events that publicize the organization and its programs to the community.
  • Trains, mentors, and supervises sponsored programs staff members, and prepares performance reports.
  • Negotiates contractual provisions with potential partners.
  • Develops and provides reports or documentation needed to secure and maintain funding and grants. Ensures that grants and contracts adhere to organizational standards.
  • Acts as department expert and primary point of contact on funding issues and disputes.
  • Establishes and continuously assesses the effectiveness of the internal controls within the unit and compliance with University policies and procedures.
  • Ensures employees are trained on controls within the function and on University policy and procedures.

Department Specific Functions

  • Demonstrate knowledge of federal regulations related to research administration, including OMB Uniform Guidance, Cost Accounting Standards (CAS), and Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR).
  • Oversee proposal submissions for an assigned portfolio of departments, faculty, and researchers to federal agencies, foundations, and industry sponsors.
  • Collaborate with faculty to develop proposal budgets, review sponsor guidelines, and coordinate the collection of required documentation to meet sponsor and Office of Research Administration (ORA) deadlines.
  • Oversee the submission of institutional training grants across the medical school, including NIH T32, R25, and R38 programs.
  • Work collaboratively within the Office of the Executive Dean for Research (EDRO) and with the departments and programs supported by RDS, including the EDRO Internal Awards Program.
  • Serve as a liaison between faculty and central administrative and compliance offices.
  • Participate in the preparation and submission of annual progress reports, including NIH Research Performance Progress Reports (RPPRs) through eRA Commons.
  • Assist faculty with post-award activities, including preparation and interpretation of financial reports, forecasting, effort distribution, and effort certification. Provide guidance on allowable and unallowable expenditures throughout the award lifecycle.
  • Work directly with the Office of Research Administration and faculty to facilitate non-funded sponsored agreements, including data use agreements (DUAs), material transfer agreements (MTAs), non-disclosure agreements (NDAs), no-cost extensions, and amendments.
  • Provide oversight and submission support for sponsor-related materials, including Just-in-Time (JIT) documents, post-submission requests, PRAMs, biosketch reviews, and other supporting documentation.
  • Manage a portfolio of faculty with responsibility for post-award activities, including financial reporting, forecasting, effort management, and compliance oversight.
  • Provide guidance on allowable and unallowable expenditures. Review and approve requisitions, expense reports, and purchase orders for assigned sponsored projects within Workday.
  • Meet regularly with faculty and respond promptly to requests, questions, and communications.
  • Maintain access to and proficiency in University of Miami financial and research administration systems, including IBIS, Workday, and Velos.
  • Complete all required ORA onboarding and continuing education programs to maintain system access and compliance requirements.
  • Perform other duties, ad hoc reporting, and special projects as assigned by Executive Dean for Research leadership. Demonstrate exceptional attention to detail and organizational skills.
  • Possess strong written and verbal communication skills

This list of duties and responsibilities is not intended to be all-inclusive and may be expanded to include other duties or responsibilities as necessary.

Bachelor’s degree in relevant field


Experience:

Minimum 7 years of relevant experience.
