jobs.title: Executive Director, Clinical Supply Management
jobs.description:
About Jade Biosciences

Jade Biosciences is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing best-in-class therapies that address critical unmet needs in autoimmune diseases. Jade’s lead candidate, JADE101, targets the cytokine APRIL, and is currently being evaluated for the treatment of immunoglobulin A nephropathy. Jade’s pipeline also includes JADE201, an afucosylated anti-BAFF-R monoclonal antibody, as well as JADE301, an anti-IFN-β monoclonal antibody. Jade was launched based on assets licensed from Paragon Therapeutics, an antibody discovery engine founded by Fairmount. For more information, visit JadeBiosciences.com and follow the Company on LinkedIn.

Role Overview

Jade is developing potentially transformational, disease-modifying therapies for people living with autoimmune diseases. With three biologics programs in the clinic and multiple ongoing studies from Phase I to Phase III, we are seeking an experienced Executive Director, Clinical Supply Management to join our CMC leadership team and make sure every patient in our trials receives the right investigational product, on time.

Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer (Head of CMC), you will own clinical supply strategy, planning and execution for all Jade programs. You will shape and scale the Clinical Supply Management function, growing and mentoring a team of internal employees and contractors, and you will lead a global network of CMOs and logistics partners supporting complex, multi-country and multi-site studies with ambitious timelines and enrollment targets.

This is a high-impact role for a self-starter who combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution. You will work closely with Clinical Operations and Clinical Development to secure supply for every planned study, help prepare the supply chain for BLA filing, launch and commercial readiness, and contribute directly to Jade’s key corporate goals.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead and build the function: Provide strategic and operational leadership for Jade’s Clinical Supply Management function. Further develop and scale the team through a combination of internal headcount and external partners, including recruiting, onboarding and mentoring team members and consultants. Develop robust business processes and SOP in close collaboration with the Quality function.
  • Define the clinical supply strategy: Develop and implement the clinical supply strategy for all Jade programs, from early-stage (Phase 1/2) through late-stage (Phase 3) development, with a forward-looking view toward BLA filing, product launch and commercial readiness.
  • Plan demand and supply: Build and maintain integrated global demand forecasts and supply plans based on protocols, enrollment projections and site activation plans. Balance drug product availability, shelf life, overage and cost, and update plans as studies evolve. Advise on potential risk and challenges to Senior Management and peer groups such as Clinical Operations and Development.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally: Partner closely with Clinical Operations and Clinical Development on study-specific supply strategies, and with Quality, Regulatory Affairs and CMC to forecast, align and continuously update supply requirements for ongoing and future studies. Develop options and recommendations for stakeholders and senior management.
  • Select and manage CMOs and suppliers: Select, contract and manage clinical supply CMOs, depots, couriers, logistics providers, and other critical suppliers. Set clear performance expectations and KPIs, and build strong partnerships that ensure quality, reliability and cost-effective supply.
  • Oversee clinical supply operations: Direct labeling, packaging, blinding, cold-chain storage and global distribution for all drug product formats, including vials, pre-filled syringes and autoinjectors. Manage comparator sourcing, expiry extensions, relabeling, returns, reconciliation and destruction.
  • Manage IRT and inventory: Define supply requirements for IRT/IxRS systems, including resupply strategies and user acceptance testing, and monitor inventory at depots and sites to prevent stock-outs and minimize waste.
  • Ensure compliance and quality: Maintain full compliance with Jade SOPs, cGMP, GDP, GCP, ICH guidelines and applicable global regulatory and import/export requirements. Partner with Quality on batch release (including QP release for EU studies), deviations and change controls, keep the function inspection-ready, and contribute to regulatory submissions (IND, IMPD, CTA).
  • Own the budget and reporting: Manage the clinical supply budget, and report regularly and concisely to stakeholders and senior management on inventory, supply and demand, changes and risks across all programs.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Life Sciences, Chemical Engineering or a related field.
  • 15+ years of progressive experience in clinical supply chain management, ideally with biologics, including significant experience leading teams. Experience in commercial supply chain management is a plus.
  • Proven experience managing clinical supply for biologics in vials within cold-chain environments, using local and multinational CMOs; experience with pre-filled syringes and combination products such as autoinjectors highly preferred.
  • Experience supporting multiple early- and late-stage programs, including multi-country Phase 3 studies and bridging studies for biologic combination products.
  • Comprehensive understanding of global regulatory and import/export requirements across Europe, North America, China, Japan and Rest of World (ROW), and strong working knowledge of cGMP, GDP and GCP.
  • Hands-on experience with IRT/IxRS systems, clinical supply forecasting tools and budget management.
  • Demonstrated success building and scaling clinical supply functions, including hiring, onboarding and managing team members and consultants to meet critical milestones.
  • Exceptional communication, leadership and interpersonal skills, with a track record of aligning CMC, Quality, Regulatory Affairs and Clinical teams and building trusting relationships with external CMO partners.
  • A strategic thinker with a proven execution record, strong problem-solving skills and the ability to thrive in a complex, fast-paced clinical development environment.

Position Location

This is a remote role; periodic travel to team and company events is required.

The anticipated salary range for candidates for this role is $280,000 - $300,000. The final salary offered will depend on several factors, which may include, but not limited to, relevant years of experience, educational background, and geography.

As part of the I-9 verification of authorization to work in the United States, Jade Bioscience participates in E-Verify. To learn more about E-Verify please review this poster.

Jade Biosciences is proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Clinical GTM Lead
jobs.description:
About Latent

Latent is the enterprise pharmacy intelligence platform, powered by a clinical agentic engine, that enables health systems to grow their pharmacy operations and serve more patients. One engine works across the pharmacy journey to identify patients who qualify for care, improve medication access, capture eligible prescriptions and support patients throughout treatment.

Latent’s platform enables more than 60+ leading health systems that collectively serve an estimated 70 million people. Founded by Sri Somasundaram and Rishabh Jain, Latent has raised $80 million from Transformation Capital, Spark Capital, Conviction, General Catalyst, Y Combinator, and others.

The Role

As Clinical GTM Lead, you will be Latent’s pharmacy subject matter expert for prospective and current customers. You’ll work with Sales on demos, clinical diligence, and executive conversations; support Partner Experience through implementations and account growth; and bring what you hear from customers back to Product. You’ll help pharmacy leaders understand how Latent fits their workflows, where it can make a difference, and how we approach clinical quality and patient safety.

Your presence should give customers confidence that experienced pharmacists help build Latent and support its products. This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys working directly with customers and turning clinical insight into practical action.

What You’ll Do

Clinical sales partnership

  • Lead the clinical portions of sales calls, product demos, diligence, and executive meetings. Address questions about pharmacy operations, medication access, and how Latent fits into existing workflows.

  • Partner with Sales to anticipate objections, explain the product clearly to clinical and nonclinical stakeholders, and build trust through accurate, direct answers.

Customer implementation and growth

  • Work with Partner Experience to understand each customer’s workflows, support implementation decisions, and help pharmacy teams adopt the product successfully.

  • Join strategic account conversations to identify opportunities for deeper use, retention, and expansion that serve customer and patient needs.

Product insight and clinical accuracy

  • Turn customer feedback and clinical requirements into clear recommendations for Product, balancing clinical value, operational feasibility, and business impact.

  • Review customer-facing claims, presentations, and guidance for clinical accuracy and sound judgment around patient safety, compliance, and product positioning.

Tools that help the team scale

  • Create reusable clinical presentations, diligence responses, workflow guidance, and answers to common customer questions.

  • Equip Sales and Partner Experience to handle recurring clinical questions confidently while knowing when to bring in deeper pharmacy expertise.

What Success Looks Like

  • Within six months: You are a trusted clinical partner on our most important sales opportunities and customer accounts, and you have built materials and processes that Sales and Partner Experience use regularly.

  • Within 12 months: Your work has strengthened clinical confidence throughout the sales process, supported retention and expansion, and established a clear feedback loop among customers, Latent’s clinical team, and Product.

What We’re Looking For

  • A PharmD from an accredited institution and an active or recently active pharmacist license in at least one U.S. state.

  • At least seven years of relevant experience across pharmacy practice, clinical operations, healthcare technology, or related work, including meaningful experience with pharmacy workflows.

  • Strong understanding of medication access and the day-to-day needs of pharmacists, pharmacy leaders, and the organizations they serve.

  • Experience working directly with customers and communicating with clinical, operational, and executive stakeholders. You can lead a detailed workflow discussion and an executive conversation with equal confidence.

  • A record of owning clinical, operational, product, or customer outcomes, with the ability to turn clinical requirements into practical solutions.

  • Clear writing and presentation skills. You make complex clinical topics understandable and create materials that other teams can use.

  • Sound judgment about clinical risk, patient safety, compliance, and the claims we make about our product.

  • Comfort learning and explaining technical and AI products, and working closely with commercial and technical teams.

  • A hands-on, low-ego approach. You take ownership, move through ambiguity, and help the team get the work done.

Nice to Have

  • Experience at a healthcare technology, digital health, or pharmacy technology company.

  • Experience supporting enterprise healthcare sales, strategic accounts, or technology implementations in a pharmacy organization.

  • Familiarity with AI products or clinical decision support tools.

  • Relationships with pharmacy executives or health system pharmacy leaders, or experience speaking at industry events.

Why Join Latent

  • Help more patients get the medications they need by improving how pharmacy teams work.

  • Work closely with Sales, Partner Experience, Product, and our clinical team on problems that matter to customers.

  • Shape how Latent earns clinical trust as the company grows, with the ownership to build what the team needs.

jobs.title: Senior Donor Relations Officer
jobs.description:
You: The champion who turns belief in liberty into the resources to defend it. Every case PLF wins starts with someone who chose to fund the fight. You'll be that person's trusted partner. You'll get to know what drives our donors, show them the real impact of their giving, and invite them to make bold investments in freedom.

Them: Bureaucrats, city councils, mayors, governors, and federal agencies stripping Americans of their rights every day. There’s a lot of government overreach out there, and it’s backed by seemingly endless resources. But fortunately, like all lumbering giants, abusive government is most vulnerable when countered by individuals who act strategically and nimbly, take calculated risks, have each other’s backs, and are confident in and passionate for the cause—the very sort of swashbucklers we employ in spades here at PLF.

Us: We fight back. Pacific Legal Foundation is the nation’s first and most successful public interest law firm dedicated to vindicating individual liberty. PLF has an unmatched record in the United States Supreme Court, with 18 victories out of 21 litigated at the Court—including three victories last term. We also have nearly two hundred active cases across the nation.

We are a next-generation public interest law firm. That means we aren’t interested in doing the same thing as everyone else. We aspire to be the best player in a constantly changing game.

Here’s what you get to do in this role:

The Senior Donor Relations Officer is responsible for developing and managing a portfolio of high-capacity current and prospective major gift donors, with responsibility for the identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of significant philanthropic relationships supporting Pacific Legal Foundation’s mission and strategic priorities.

The Senior Donor Relations Officer will develop and execute sophisticated donor strategies, build meaningful long-term relationships with donors and prospects, and secure significant new, renewed, and increased philanthropic commitments.

The successful candidate will be an accomplished frontline fundraiser with exceptional relationship-building and communication skills, strong fundraising judgment, and a demonstrated record of closing significant major gifts. The position requires a highly organized, persistent, disciplined, and self-directed professional who can operate with substantial independence while collaborating effectively with PLF leadership, attorneys, and Development colleagues.

Getting down to brass tacks, your specific job duties likely will include:

  • Managing a portfolio of approximately 100 high-capacity major gift donors and prospects and achieve established fundraising, engagement, and solicitation goals.
  • Developing and executing individualized strategies for donor qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
  • Personally soliciting and securing significant new, renewed, and increased gifts, including six-figure and seven-figure commitments.
  • Building trusted, long-term donor relationships by understanding donors’ interests, motivations, and philanthropic priorities and serving as their primary PLF relationship manager.
  • Creating meaningful donor engagement and stewardship opportunities that demonstrate the impact of philanthropy and connect donors to PLF’s litigation, policy, and strategic priorities.
  • Strategically engaging PLF executives, attorneys, trustees, and other organizational leaders in donor cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
  • Identifying and advancing new major gift prospects and recognize opportunities for multi-year, planned, blended, campaign, and other complex gifts in collaboration with Development colleagues.
  • Maintaining a disciplined portfolio and moves management, including donor strategies, next steps, solicitation plans, revenue projections, contact reports, and accurate CRM records.
  • Contributing to Development team strategy and serve as a resource to colleagues on complex donor relationships and major gift opportunities.

The ideal candidate will have:

  • 8+ years of professional fundraising experience, including substantial frontline major gift experience.
  • A demonstrated record of personally cultivating, soliciting, and closing significant major gifts, preferably including six and seven figure commitments.
  • Exceptional interpersonal, listening, verbal, and written communication skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships and communicate complex ideas clearly and compellingly.
  • Strong strategic judgment, initiative, organization, and personal accountability, with the ability to operate independently in a results-oriented environment.
  • Proficiency with fundraising CRM systems and disciplined portfolio and moves management practices.
  • A willingness to travel up to 50% throughout the United States, with a heavy focus throughout California, to meet with donors and prospects.
  • A sincere appreciation for PLF’s mission

Preferred experience. Previous experience with a pro-liberty organization, legal advocacy organization, public policy organization, or similar mission-driven institution is a plus. Experience with Salesforce or a comparable fundraising CRM is also preferred.

General information:

Pacific Legal Foundation identifies and litigates important legal issues to set landmark precedents that will benefit Americans nationwide. Using strategic and principled litigation, communications, and research, we battle for freedom in the nation’s courts and the court of public opinion.

As a national nonprofit organization, PLF has brick-and-mortar offices in Sacramento, California and Arlington, Virginia, although approximately half of the staff work from home offices across the country. You may work from any of our offices or request to work remotely, although strong preference will be given to California-based candidates.

Salary range and benefits:

This is a full-time, permanent position. PLF is committed to recruiting and retaining the highest-quality talent available nationwide, and we offer a total compensation package that includes a competitive salary, medical and dental insurance, and employer-paid retirement savings. We take work-life balance seriously through our generous paid leave and flextime policies. To learn more about the starting salary range and benefits options, please apply.

How to apply:

Qualified candidates should submit the following application materials:

  • Résumé
  • Cover letter detailing the candidate’s sincere interest in Pacific Legal Foundation, its mission, and the Senior Donor Relations Officer position

jobs.title: Associate Director, Development Outsourcing
jobs.description:
About Jade Biosciences

Jade Biosciences is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing best-in-class therapies that address critical unmet needs in autoimmune diseases. Jade’s lead candidate, JADE101, targets the cytokine APRIL, and is currently being evaluated for the treatment of immunoglobulin A nephropathy. Jade’s pipeline also includes JADE201, an afucosylated anti-BAFF-R monoclonal antibody, as well as JADE301, an anti-IFN-β monoclonal antibody. Jade was launched based on assets licensed from Paragon Therapeutics, an antibody discovery engine founded by Fairmount. For more information, visit JadeBiosciences.com and follow the Company on LinkedIn.

Role Overview

As the Associate Director of Development Outsourcing, you will play a key role in supporting the sourcing and strategic management of Jade's external vendors. This role will partner closely with Development Operations and study teams to support vendor sourcing, contracting, governance, and the development of strong vendor relationships across clinical development programs from Phase I through Phase IV.

The successful candidate will work cross-functionally to drive effective execution, support issue resolution, and contribute to continuous improvement of Development Outsourcing processes. This newly created role will report to the Director, Development outsourcing. This is a fully remote role and will require occasional travel.

Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as the primary Development Outsourcing lead for assigned studies and programs, partnering closely with cross-functional study teams and external vendors to ensure successful execution of outsourcing activities.
  • Implement outsourcing strategies and plans established by Development Outsourcing leadership while independently managing day-to-day vendor-related activities for assigned studies.
  • Provide outsourcing expertise and recommendations to study teams regarding vendor selection, contract strategy, oversight, and issue resolution.
  • Ensure outsourcing deliverables, timelines, and decisions are executed efficiently and aligned with study objectives.
  • Lead vendor sourcing and evaluation activities in support of Development Programs, including preparation of RFI/RFP materials, proposal review, bid defense coordination, comparative analyses, and recommendation development.
  • Lead the development, negotiation, and execution of vendor agreements, including Confidentiality Agreements, Master Service Agreements, Statements of Work, Change Orders, rate cards, Letters of Intent, and other vendor-related agreements.
  • Partner with Legal, Finance, and study teams to drive contract execution and resolve business or operational issues impacting study startup or execution.
  • Act as the day-to-day outsourcing representative for assigned vendors and studies, proactively identifying and resolving operational issues, risks, and decisions.
  • Escalate significant risks, relationship concerns, performance issues, or strategic decisions to Development Outsourcing leadership while driving follow-through on agreed actions.
  • Support vendor governance activities by preparing materials, tracking actions, monitoring performance metrics, and ensuring commitments are executed.
  • Monitor vendor performance and support implementation of corrective and preventive actions when needed.
  • Partner closely with Development Operations, Clinical Quality Assurance, Legal, Finance, and other stakeholders to ensure effective vendor oversight and execution.
  • Support vendor qualification, audit readiness, inspection preparedness, and oversight activities in collaboration with Clinical Quality Assurance.
  • Maintain documentation related to vendor selection, contracting, governance, performance management, and issue resolution.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement of Development Outsourcing processes, tools, templates, and best practices.
  • Operate effectively in a fast-paced, evolving environment by balancing urgent issues, strategic priorities, and routine responsibilities across multiple concurrent activities.
  • Exercise sound judgment and independent decision-making when addressing operational challenges, while recognizing when leadership engagement or escalation is required.
  • Demonstrate initiative and accountability by driving decisions, resolving obstacles, and ensuring commitments are completed.

Qualifications

  • 8-12 years of biotechnology, pharmaceutical, CRO, or contract research experience with significant experience in Development Outsourcing, Clinical Operations, Vendor Management, or a related function.
  • Strong understanding of clinical development and outsourced service delivery models across Phases I-IV.
  • Demonstrated experience leading vendor sourcing initiatives, RFP processes, bid defenses, contract negotiations, and vendor oversight activities.
  • Experience negotiating and managing Master Service Agreements, Statements of Work, Change Orders, and other vendor-related contracts.
  • Proven ability to independently manage complex outsourcing activities across multiple studies and stakeholders.
  • Strong business judgment, organizational skills, and ability to prioritize effectively in a dynamic environment.
  • Ability to identify risks, make timely decisions, and drive resolution of issues with limited direction.
  • Strong communication, negotiation, influence, and relationship management skills.
  • Experience collaborating effectively within cross-functional and matrixed organizations.

Position Location

This is a remote role; periodic travel to team and company events is required.

The anticipated salary range for candidates for this role is $175,000 - $190,000. The final salary offered will depend on several factors, which may include, but not limited to, relevant years of experience, educational background, and geography.

As part of the I-9 verification of authorization to work in the United States, Jade Bioscience participates in E-Verify. To learn more about E-Verify please review this poster.

Jade Biosciences is proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Behind the user-friendly iOS and Android apps and webpage that work across the world is the engineering team. We are in charge of creating, developing, improving, and maintaining all Fever services so that more people can have an amazing experience.

About the role

Location: Spain - 100% Home office friendly

What are we looking for:

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join the Engineering team with outstanding software development talent proven by great work results/experience. Somebody who cares about code quality and not just getting things done, but getting things done right.

If you're smart, have great energy, can't think about a system without a CI/CD pipeline, and you want to thrive in a fast-paced environment, we are in sync.

  • Meet your buddy and team, and get to know Fever’s culture and ways of working.
  • Set up your local environment and become familiar with our Python-based stack, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud infrastructure.

  • Lead by example through code reviews, design sessions, and mentoring.
  • Contribute to best practices in areas like scalability, observability, and system design.
  • Drive continuous improvement and have a visible impact on how we build high-performing services at scale.

Must have skills:

  • You are proficient in business English
  • You know how to deliver code from development to production
  • Experience with RESTful APIs (implementation and consumption)
  • Knowledge of relational databases and SQL
  • Experience with event streaming platforms such as Kafka or RabbitMQ
  • Handling services with high concurrencies and high volume requests.

We use these technologies, so it would be a plus if you have experience in:

  • Django/Flask
  • PostgreSQL and Redis
  • AWS, Docker, and Kubernetes

Benefits & Perks

  • 23 days of vacation plus half a day on your birthday
  • Private medical insurance sponsored by the company
  • 40% discount on Fever Marketplace
  • Flexibility to work from home
  • English & Spanish conversational classes

  • Possibility to receive part of your salary in advance with Payflow

    • Base Salary: 50K - 75K EUR
    • Total Compensation: 67K - 90K EUR (Including Base, Variable, and Stock Options)

About the process

Fever aims to provide the best and fastest possible experience to our candidates. This is how it would look like:

  • Talent Interview - 1h: An intro to Fever, our culture and a conversation about your background and experience.
  • Technical Interview - 2h: A deep dive into your technical expertise through a system design discussion and a short coding exercise, giving you the chance to walk us through your reasoning and problem-solving approach — and ask us anything about your day-to-day at Fever.

jobs.title: Sr. Software Engineer, Cloud Platform
jobs.description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

As a Senior Engineer in the Infrastructure org, you will help evolve the cloud foundations behind every Samsara product. Your goal will be to reduce systemic production risk and enable continued growth by making infrastructure safer to change, easier to operate, and more resilient and cost-efficient at scale.

You will bring deep expertise in at least one infrastructure domain, such as compute and workload orchestration, networking, storage and stateful systems, or cloud control planes, and apply it across our multi-account, multi-region AWS environment. You will lead work such as modernizing compute and stateful infrastructure, strengthening capacity and failure isolation, and building standardized infrastructure-as-code workflows and reusable automation.

You will partner with product engineering teams to turn recurring risks and manual operations into durable platforms and paved paths. We do not expect you to be an expert in every infrastructure domain. We are looking for engineers who have built and operated critical systems at significant scale, understand how infrastructure fails, and can use that experience to improve both our platforms and our engineering practices.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: The software, firmware, and hardware you build will result in real-world impact, helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • You are a life-long learner: We have ambitious goals. Every Samsarian has a growth mindset as we work with a wide range of technologies, challenges, and customers that push us to learn on the go.
  • You believe customers are more than a number: Samsara engineers enjoy a rare closeness to the end user and you will have the opportunity to participate in customer interviews, collaborate with customer success and product managers, and use metrics to ensure our work is translating into better customer outcomes.
  • You are a team player: Working on our Samsara Engineering teams requires a mix of independent effort and collaboration. Motivated by our mission, we’re all racing toward our connected operations vision, and we intend to win together.

In this role, you will:

  • Design, build, and operate reliable cloud platforms, bringing depth in one or more areas such as compute, networking, storage, stateful systems, or infrastructure control planes.
  • Improve the scalability, capacity management, isolation, recovery, and cost efficiency of critical production infrastructure.
  • Build standardized infrastructure-as-code workflows and reusable automation that support self-service provisioning, testing, progressive rollout, reconciliation, rollback, and drift prevention.
  • Identify shared failure modes and build safeguards that prevent localized failures from escalating into broad customer impact.
  • Contribute to multi-account, multi-region, and isolated AWS architectures, including regulated environments such as GovCloud.
  • Participate in operational ownership and incident response, using incidents and near misses to drive durable architectural improvements.
  • Mentor engineers, raise the quality of infrastructure design and operational judgment, and establish patterns that can be adopted across the organization.
  • Clearly communicate architecture, trade-offs, risks, and migration plans to technical and organizational stakeholders.
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices.

Minimum requirements for this role.

  • 6+ years of experience designing and building software, infrastructure, or distributed systems, including operating critical systems in production.
  • Deep expertise in at least one of the following: compute and workload orchestration, networking, storage and stateful systems, or cloud infrastructure control planes.
  • Strong software-engineering fundamentals in Go, Python, Java, or a similar language.
  • Hands-on experience designing and operating infrastructure on a major public cloud platform; AWS experience is preferred.
  • Experience using infrastructure as code, such as Terraform, to safely manage production infrastructure.
  • Strong understanding of capacity management, failure domains, observability, rollout safety, and production recovery.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex technical initiatives across teams and through ambiguous problem spaces.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Designing and operating large-scale compute or container platforms such as ECS, EKS, Kubernetes, or similar orchestration systems.
  • Designing and operating stateful distributed systems such as Kafka, OpenSearch, managed databases, caching, or large-scale storage platforms.
  • Building internal infrastructure platforms, control planes, or self-service developer experiences adopted across multiple teams.
  • Designing multi-account or multi-region cloud architectures with strong workload isolation and disaster recovery.
  • Leading major infrastructure migrations while maintaining availability and controlling operational risk.
  • Delivering measurable improvements in infrastructure capacity, cost efficiency, or developer self-service.

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email accessibleinterviewing@samsara.com or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our blog post here.

jobs.description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

The Senior Security Engineer – Enterprise Security shares ownership of the day-to-day operation of the Samsara security environment. You will keep our network access, device trust, and visibility systems running, tuned, and resilient at enterprise scale in partnership with a global team. Utilizing modern principles, you’ll maintain and evolve a modern zero trust program, spend time both on policy design and real-time triage for escalations.

You take security seriously and believe the best solutions are low-friction and built in partnership with others. You are comfortable owning and maintaining production systems for long term success - troubleshooting systemic issues, tuning policies based on real incidents, and continuously improving what is already built. You bring an automation mindset to repetitive work, whether using Python, SOAR platforms, or AI-assisted tools. You enjoy supporting teammates and helping other engineers build their security knowledge.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the United Kingdom. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.

About this team:

Enterprise Security is a global team spanning the US, EMEA, and India. We work in close partnership with our coworkers as collaborators rather than gatekeepers. Leadership is hands-on and technical, and our culture encourages everyone to contribute across the full stack.

Executive leadership actively champions security as a competitive advantage that builds customer trust and helps win enterprise partnerships. You will see a direct line between the zero trust systems you operate and the security that protects our physical operations partners worldwide. Our on-call rotation for the highest severity incidents is spread evenly across the team for one week out of every ten.

In this role, you will:

  • Co-own the day-to-day operation, triage, and tuning of the Samsara endpoint security environment by responding to escalations, investigating anomalies, and resolving issues
  • Continuously improve existing endpoint visibility tools and workflows in partnership with our Security Operations team, and based on real usage patterns and incident learnings
  • Write clear, concise documentation and runbooks for enterprise security workflows
  • Collaborate with partners across Engineering, IT, and Security to ensure proper implementation of security tools and policies
  • Assist the Security Operations team during security investigations, acting as a technical subject matter expert within your domain
  • Partner with engineering teams to triage and support remediation of vulnerabilities and misconfigurations
  • Mentor engineers on the Security team to grow their domain knowledge, tool-specific skills, and communication abilities
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team)

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 5+ years of relevant experience in an Enterprise Security role with demonstrated impact
  • Hands-on experience operating and maintaining endpoint security and visibility tools at enterprise scale (e.g. Crowdstrike, osquery, or similar)
  • Exposure to at least one additional enterprise security tool stack beyond endpoint security, such as Secure Access Service Edge (SASE), zero trust systems, email security, Data Loss Prevention (DLP), or Identity and Access Management (IAM)
  • An automation mindset with experience scripting and debugging code with Python (with or without AIassistance) and using SOAR platforms
  • Strong familiarity with common security challenges and the ability to independently evaluate their severity and business impact
  • Track record of delivering impactful work across multiple quarters and collaborating effectively across teams

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Significant breadth across the endpoint security ecosystem, including designing layered controls with EDR tools, passive telemetry, integration with threat intelligence feeds, and operation in cloud and containerized environments.
  • History of building out security programs using modern SaaS security platforms such as Crowdstrike, Mimecast Incydr, and Splunk
  • Experience with infrastructure as code deployments using Terraform
  • Experience with AI-driven automations

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

jobs.title: Assistant Site Manager - Events (Bristol)
jobs.description:
Hey there!
We’re Fever, the world’s leading tech platform for culture and live entertainment.

Our mission? To democratize access to culture and entertainment. With our proprietary cutting-edge technology and data-driven approach, we’re revolutionizing the way people engage with live entertainment.

Every month, our platform inspires over 300 million people in +55 countries (and counting) to discover unforgettable experiences while also empowering event creators with our data and technology, helping them scale, innovate, and enhance their events to reach new audiences.

Our results? We’ve teamed up with major industry leaders like Netflix, F.C. Barcelona, and Primavera Sound, presented international award-winning experiences, and are backed by several leading global investors! Impressive, right?

To achieve our mission, we are looking for bar-raisers with a hands-on mindset who are eager to help shape the future of entertainment!

Ready to be part of the experience?

Now, let’s discuss this role and what you will do to help achieve Fever’s mission.

Assistant Site Manager - VR Concept Venue

Location: Bristol
Contract: Freelance, September 2026 – March 2027 (potential to extend)
Pay: £16 per hour
Working Pattern: Full-time (job share considered); requires evenings, weekends, and public holiday availability. Shift pattern arranged to overlap with, and to cover for, the Event Manager (Site Manager) as needed.
Reports to: Charlotte Potter, Producer – Fever (day-to-day line management from the Event Manager / Site Manager)
Manages: Front-of-house staff (agency and in-house); full management responsibility for all staff, including cleaners and front-of-house teams, when covering for the Event Manager during periods of leave

Role Overview
We're looking for a proactive and technically confident Assistant Site Manager to support the day-to-day running of our immersive VR experience in a high-footfall Bristol venue. Working closely with the Event Manager, you'll help keep the visitor experience running smoothly, staff well supported, and systems fully
operational.

This role also acts as key holiday and absence cover for the Event Manager (Site Manager), stepping up to take full responsibility for the venue — technical, operational, and people management — whenever they are away. You'll need the confidence to run the site independently at short notice, alongside your regular assistant duties.

Key Responsibilities

🔧 Technical & Operational Delivery
● Support daily setup and shutdown of the VR experience, ensuring all systems, hardware, and software are fully operational.
● Carry out pre-opening checks (hardware calibration, environment readiness, content testing) alongside or in place of the Event Manager.
● Troubleshoot first-line IT and technical issues on-site (VR headsets, PCs, networking, displays), escalating to tech support partners where needed.
● Monitor experience performance throughout the day, resolving disruptions or resets promptly.
● Maintain stock of consumables (e.g., sanitisation wipes, headset liners) and uphold hygiene protocols.
● Assist in keeping technical documentation up to date and support training of team members on troubleshooting procedures.

🏛 Venue Operations (Ground Floor)
● Help ensure the ground floor VR experience space is clean, safe, and visitor-ready at all times.
● Coordinate cleaning and reactive maintenance for the VR zone, including public and back-of-house areas.
● Support queue management, timed entry, and visitor flow, particularly during peak periods.

👥 Team Support & Holiday Cover
● Assist in line managing front-of-house staff, including agency team members, day to day.
● Support daily staff briefings, rota coordination, and shift cover.
● Model high standards of customer service and professionalism for the wider team.
● Help train new team members on VR-specific procedures, safety, and technical protocols.
● Take full ownership of team management, rotas, and briefings during any period covering for the Event Manager, ensuring continuity of standards and cover.

🛡 Health & Safety
● Support daily safety and cleanliness walkarounds of the VR area.
● Act as a trained first aider for the venue, leading incident response (first aid, equipment malfunctions, or guest complaints), including full responsibility for this when covering for the Event Manager.
● Help keep risk assessments for the VR zone up to date and log incidents or near misses.
● Ensure staff are trained in relevant H&S procedures, including emergency evacuations and manual handling (if required).

📣 Customer Experience
● Help maintain a welcoming, engaging, and inclusive atmosphere for all guests.
● Act as a point of escalation for visitor queries or complaints, and the main escalation point when covering for the Event Manager.
● Support customer feedback mechanisms and feed insights back to the Producer and Event Manager.

📝 Communication & Reporting
● Provide handovers to the Event Manager (or, during cover periods, directly to the Producer) covering technical issues, visitor numbers, and operational highlights.
● Maintain accurate logs: staff attendance, incident reports, daily checklists, and maintenance tickets.
● Ensure a clean handover back to the Event Manager after any period of holiday cover, flagging anything requiring follow-up.

Ideal Candidate Profile
● Current, valid First Aid at Work certification is required for this role.
● Experience in live event, visitor attraction, or venue operations — preferably in immersive or tech-driven environments.
● Working knowledge of VR hardware/software and basic IT troubleshooting (e.g., Windows PCs, networks, Wi-Fi, device calibration).
● Experience supporting or managing teams, including casual/agency staff, in high-traffic public settings.
● Comfortable stepping up to run a site independently at short notice, with strong organisational skills and a calm, solutions-focused approach under pressure.
● Confident communicator and team player who thrives in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.
● Working knowledge of health & safety regulations and customer service best practices.

Additional Info
● Flexibility is essential: early starts, late finishes, and public holidays are part of the standard schedule.
● Some Mondays/Tuesdays may be required for maintenance, special events, or staff training.
● Holiday cover for the Event Manager should be expected on a periodic basis throughout the contract; specific dates to be agreed and scheduled in advance where possible.

jobs.title: Director of Platform Engineering [gn] Data Intelligence Platform
jobs.description:
Actian is the company behind the Data Intelligence Platform — an enterprise solution that helps organisations discover, govern, and trust their data at scale. Our platform connects metadata, data lineage, data quality, and business context into a single knowledge graph, enabling enterprises to turn raw data into reliable decisions. We operate globally, move fast, and build for the long term.

Software engineering is being redefined. The engineers who will shape the next decade of product development are not the ones who write the most code — they are the ones who know how to think clearly, ship confidently, and use every tool available to them, including AI, to multiply their impact.

The Actian Data Intelligence Platform helps teams find, understand, and use AI-ready data under clear governance. It connects metadata, data lineage, data quality, and business context into a single knowledge graph, so enterprises can turn raw data into reliable decisions — the trusted foundation that AI agents increasingly depend on to work. We operate globally, move fast, and build for the long term.

The Data Intelligence Platform has to deploy, operate, and pass audits in every one of the environments our customers run — public cloud, private cloud, and on-premises. We are standing up a dedicated platform team to make that possible, and we are hiring the leader who will build it.

This is a hands-on director role. You will stand up and lead a newly formed platform team, hire and grow it, and build alongside it from day one: you will design the platform services, write infrastructure code, and set the engineering standards the rest of engineering relies on.

We are an AI-first engineering organization, and in this role AI is how the work gets done. AI agents run operational tasks, AI accelerates the team's own engineering, and AI replaces tools we pay for today but no longer need. You will also build the infrastructure that runs the AI and ML workloads inside our product.

What You Will Own:

  • Platform services for the Data Intelligence Platform, including the infrastructure behind the data catalog, the knowledge graph, and the APIs that power customer integrations.

  • Cloud-agnostic deployment of the Platform across AWS, a second public cloud (Azure or Google Cloud), and customer on-premises and private-cloud environments — including packaging, installation, upgrades, and supportability.

  • The internal developer platform and CI/CD, including GitOps delivery, so engineering teams ship safely and quickly.

  • Security operations and compliance evidence for SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and GDPR — including EU data residency — in partnership with the security team.

  • Cloud cost management and FinOps, with clear cost visibility and accountability across every environment.

  • Infrastructure for the AI and ML workloads used by the Platform.

  • Observability, reliability, and incident response for the services the team runs, including the team's on-call rotation.

  • Building and growing the team — hiring platform engineers, setting the operating model, and establishing the standards and rituals the team works by.

What You Will Deliver in Your First 12 Months:

  • High-functioning platform team: an operating model in place, and clear ownership boundaries with the product engineering teams you serve.

  • Portable, cloud-agnostic deployments: one deployment model that runs the Platform on AWS, on at least one other cloud, and on customer infrastructure — defined as code and delivered through GitOps.

  • AI agents running operations: agents that handle routine operational work — triage, remediation, change validation, and reporting — with measurable reductions in manual effort and a smaller tool footprint.

  • Platform foundations for the data catalog, the knowledge graph, and integration APIs: scalable, observable infrastructure that product teams build on.

  • Compliance automation and audit readiness: evidence for SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and GDPR collected automatically from the platform rather than assembled by hand before each audit.

We expect this leader to treat AI as part of the platform. That means you will:

  • Design and run AI agents that operate infrastructure under clear guardrails — human approval for high-risk changes, and full audit trails.

  • Review our current tooling and retire tools that AI agents or simpler automation can replace, with a cost and risk case for each change.

  • Use AI coding and operations assistants in your own daily work, and set the standard for how the team uses them.

  • Build the compute, data, and access patterns that let AI and ML workloads run reliably in every environment we support.

What You Bring:

  • 10+ years in platform engineering, infrastructure, DevOps, or SRE, including 3+ years managing engineers — with experience building or scaling a team, not only running an established one.

  • AI-first mindset, making extensive use of this technology for accelerating developments.

  • A track record of shipping on-premises or self-hosted software that customers install and run in their own environments.

  • Deep, hands-on experience with Kubernetes in production, infrastructure as code (Terraform/Terragrunt), and GitOps delivery with Argo CD or similar tooling.

  • Strong AWS experience, and the judgment to design for portability rather than lock-in to a single cloud.

  • Hands-on experience operating systems under SOC 2, ISO 27001, and GDPR controls, including data-residency requirements.

  • Experience managing cloud costs and making cost trade-offs explicit to engineering and business leaders.

  • Clear written communication, suited to a fully remote team across US and EU time zones.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience running infrastructure for data platforms, data catalogs, or graph databases.

  • Production experience on Azure or Google Cloud in addition to AWS.

  • Experience with air-gapped or restricted-network customer deployments.

  • Experience building infrastructure for AI and ML workloads, including model serving and vector or graph data stores.

  • Observability with OpenTelemetry or comparable tooling, from instrumentation through alerting.

  • Privileged access management with StrongDM or a comparable tool.

What We Value:

We value autonomy over process, outcomes over activity, and builders over theorists. This role suits someone who thrives when handed a hard problem, a team to build, and the space to figure it out — and who uses every tool available, including AI, to multiply the team's impact.

How You Will Work:

You will report to the SVP of Engineering and work closely with product engineering, security, customer success, and support. The role is fully remote from the US, UK, Spain, France or Germany, with at least four hours a day of overlap with both US Eastern Time and Central European Time. Expect occasional travel for team offsites and company-wide meetings.

What We Offer:

  • The chance to be part of an innovative, fast-growing company making a significant impact in the data management space.
  • Collaboration with a passionate and diverse team.
  • Competitive salary and benefits package.
  • Flexible work arrangements (remote or hybrid).
  • Opportunities for professional growth and development.

Compensation

Additional Information

Why Join Us? At Actian, we are passionate about innovation and teamwork. This role is perfect for someone who thrives in a dynamic environment, loves creating an efficient and welcoming workspace, and enjoys working closely with a talented team.

Interested? We’d love to hear from you! Let’s discuss how you can contribute to our success while growing your career with us.

We value diversity at our company. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or any other applicable legally protected characteristics in the location in which the candidate is applying.

jobs.description:
What Cognite is: Relentless to achieve

Cognite operates at the forefront of industrial digitalization, building AI, and data solutions that solve the world’s hardest, highest-impact problems. With unmatched industrial heritage and a comprehensive suite of AI capabilities, including low-code AI agents, Cognite accelerates the digital transformation to drive operational improvements.

We thrive in challenges. We challenge assumptions. We execute with speed and ownership. If you view obstacles as signals to step forward - not backwards - you’ll feel right at home here.

Our Moonshot is bold: Unlock $100B in customer value by 2035, and redefine how global industry works. Join us in this venture where AI and data meet ingenuity, and together, we will forge the path to a smarter, more connected industrial future.

Location: Field / Remote

Travel: Approximately 50% (Client sites & Norway office)

About Cognite

Cognite is a global industrial Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) company enabling the full-scale digital transformation of heavy-asset industries. Our core software product, Cognite Data Fusion (CDF), powers companies with contextualized OT/IT data to develop and scale solutions that increase safety, sustainability, and operational efficiency while driving revenue.

Role Overview

As a Business Development Director within our Supply Chain Center of Excellence (CoE), you will drive Cognite’s growth by winning new Supply Chain business within accounts headquartered in your territory. Operating as a subject matter expert, you will leverage deep domain insights to help customers transform their supply chain value chain using Cognite Applications and the Cognite Data Fusion Platform.

Key Responsibilities

  • Territory & CoE Strategy: Develop and execute a targeted territory strategy to accelerate bookings growth and secure high-impact supply chain clients.
  • Pipeline Generation: Actively prospect and leverage your personal network to generate pipeline, providing compelling "commercial insights" on optimizing the supply chain value chain.
  • Complex Sales Execution: Lead extended territory teams (including pre-sales and technical experts) through complex enterprise sales cycles to exceed bookings targets.
  • Value-Based Selling: Quantify ROI and present strong business cases to help enterprise executives justify software investments.
  • Partner-savvy: work with partners to qualify and progress their pipeline, and drive joint engagements on qualified opportunities.
  • Deal Negotiation: Support the Account / Engagement Leader in negotiating favorable pricing and commercial terms with C-level executives by demonstrating the long-term strategic value of Cognite’s solutions.

This is a Player/Coach role. Why 6sense?

  • Own the Core Predictive Foundation. Personally drive the strategy for our core models. You will define the roadmap for how these models are consumed by downstream applications across the entire 6sense ecosystem.
  • Drive Cross-Model Initiatives. Establish the global standards and methodologies for ongoing model training, feedback loops, and accuracy measurement to ensure our predictions remain the industry benchmark.

jobs.title: Lead Security Systems Solutions Engineer
jobs.description:
Position Overview

We are looking for an experienced Lead Security Systems Solutions Engineer to be embedded at a leading global technology and entertainment company.

The Lead Security Systems Solutions Engineer owns the architecture and technical direction of our client's security technology ecosystem and leads the Solutions Engineering (SE) team that designs, integrates, and supports it. This role combines deep systems administration and integration expertise with project and program leadership, serving as the primary point of contact for all SE work and overseeing each project from intake through completion.

This is a full-time remote position offering competitive benefits and approximately 15% regional travel.

Essential Job Functions

Architecture & Technical Leadership

  • Own system design and integrations across the security technology ecosystem, ensuring it scales securely with the business.
  • Evaluate and select technologies, build proofs of concept, and lead adoption of emerging security technologies, including cloud camera analytics and AI-driven tools.
  • Define and enforce technical standards, architectural patterns, and security and data protection requirements.
  • Serve as technical advisor for support escalations and as SME for access control, video security, and analytics.

Project & Program Management

  • Serve as the primary intake point for all SE projects, triaging and prioritizing requests.
  • Participate in project design and scoping, leading discovery discussions to align business goals with technical realities.
  • Assign projects to Solutions Engineers (SE's) and oversee each one through completion, keeping delivery on time, within scope, and aligned to strategic objectives.
  • Manage the SE program portfolio: roadmap, priorities, dependencies, and status reporting to leadership.
  • Own resource allocation and workload balancing across the SE team, and mentor engineers throughout delivery.
  • Flag technical, operational, and security risks before they become roadblocks.

Integration, Automation & Operations

  • Architect and maintain integrations between security platforms (access control, VMS, visitor management) and enterprise systems, including legacy systems.
  • Design ETL workflows that turn security data into business intelligence.
  • Identify and deploy automation to remove repetitive manual work.
  • Lead upgrades, enhancements, and migrations; ensure uptime through proactive maintenance, troubleshooting, and root cause analysis.
  • Maintain technical documentation, architecture diagrams, SOPs, and training materials.
  • Partner with Security Operations, IT, Engineering, Product, and business stakeholders, and present complex concepts clearly to non-technical audiences.

Required Skills and Experience

  • 8+ years experience programming and administering enterprise, multi-site physical security systems.

  • 3+ years experience in a security systems architecture or technical leadership role.

  • Genetec Synergis SC-STC-001 and/or SC-ETC-001 certification.

  • Hands-on experience deploying, integrating, and supporting physical security technologies.

  • Proven project/program management experience, including intake, scoping, resource allocation, and delivering multiple concurrent projects with minimal supervision.

  • Experience building PoCs, making technology selection decisions, and mentoring engineers.

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills.

  • Studio production, entertainment, or technology industry experience.

Compensation

jobs.title: Head of Technology & Data Partnerships
jobs.description:
Our Mission:

6sense's mission is to multiply what matters: growth, retention, and efficiency. We envision a future where companies, teams and people reach their full potential.

Our People:

People are the heart and soul of 6sense. We serve with passion and purpose. We live by our Being 6sense values of Win as One Team, Stay Curious, Do The Right Thing, Own the Outcome, and Create Belonging. Every 6sensor plays a part in deﬁning the future of our industry-leading technology. 6sense is a place where difference-makers roll up their sleeves, take risks, act with integrity, and measure success by the value we create for our customers. We want 6sense to be the best chapter of your career.

The Opportunity

This is an enterprise-level leadership role responsible for defining and leading the company’s technology, data, and AI partnership strategy.

The role will serve as the executive owner of the broader technology and data partnership ecosystem.

This is not a traditional channel or alliances sales role. The focus is on partnerships that shape the product, strengthen the company’s data advantage, and extend the reach of the platform.

The leader will help determine where the company should build, buy, partner, or potentially acquire capabilities.

What the Leader Will Own

  • Set the company-wide strategy for technology, data, platform, integration, and AI partnerships.
  • Identify a focused portfolio of high-impact partnership opportunities that can improve product differentiation, innovation, distribution, and growth.
  • Build trusted C-suite relationships with priority technology platforms, data providers, cloud companies, and emerging AI ecosystems.
  • Originate and negotiate complex, multi-year agreements covering product scope, data rights, intellectual property, economics, investment, exclusivity, and governance.
  • Shape the external data strategy, including data coverage, quality, identity, signals, licensing, and differentiated data products.
  • Influence product and platform strategy by bringing an external ecosystem and market perspective into company investment decisions.
  • Partner closely with Product and Engineering to ensure strategic agreements translate into funded roadmaps, clear ownership, successful launches, and measurable customer adoption.
  • Establish portfolio governance, performance measures, and an operating model that allows the partnership capability to scale.
  • Build and develop a senior, globally effective organization over time.

Why the Role Matters

The company’s advantage depends on connecting high-quality data, identity, and signals with the platforms, data environments, and AI ecosystems where customers already work.

These partnerships are viewed as a company-level lever for product innovation, differentiation, distribution, and growth, rather than simply a source of partner-sourced revenue.

The successful leader will have significant influence over product direction, ecosystem positioning, investment choices, and how the company creates long-term strategic advantage.

What Success Looks Like

In the first 60 days

  • Assess the existing portfolio, market landscape, strategic gaps, team capabilities, active commitments, and role boundaries.

By 90 days

  • Develop an executive-ready technology, data, and AI ecosystem strategy with a concentrated set of priority bets, investment choices, executive sponsors, and Product and R&D commitments.

Within six months

  • Demonstrate visible progress on consequential partnerships, including signed or late-stage agreements with funded productization paths and clear measures of impact.

Within 12 months

  • Establish a focused portfolio producing measurable adoption, distribution, differentiation, and commercial impact, supported by trusted C-suite relationships and a scalable team and operating model.

The Profile That Will Be Successful

  • An executive who has built or materially scaled a technology, platform, product, or data partnership capability.
  • Someone who combines ecosystem strategy with enough technical fluency to engage credibly on architecture, APIs, data rights, identity, security, privacy, and AI.
  • A sophisticated negotiator who understands partnership structures, economics, data licensing, commercialization, and joint product delivery.
  • A strong cross-functional leader who can align senior Product, Engineering, commercial, legal, finance, and executive stakeholders around difficult investment and roadmap choices.
  • Someone with a practical understanding of how AI, agents, and MCP are changing enterprise software ecosystems.
  • A builder who can create the strategy, operating model, governance, metrics, and leadership team required for the capability to scale.

Base Salary Range: $195,000.00 - $270,000.00. The base salary range represents the anticipated low and high end of the base salary range for this position. Actual salaries may vary and may be above or below the range based on various factors, including but not limited to work location and experience. The base salary is one component of 6sense’s total compensation package for this position. Other compensation may include a bonus program or commission plan, and stock options if approved by 6sense’s board. In addition, 6sense provides a variety of benefits, including generous health insurance coverage, life, and disability insurance, a 401K employer matching program, paid holidays, self-care days, and paid time off (PTO).
